a135.speaker: Mahmoud Ma’alin Abdulle, Commissioner of the Somali Disaster Management Agency
a135.name: Mahmoud Ma’alin Abdulle
a135.title: Commissioner of the Somali Disaster Management Agency
a135.speech: Expressed his gratitude for the warm welcome, hospitality, and high-level farewell accorded to the Somali delegation ; emphasized the importance of continued close cooperation between the two governments in areas of humanitarian activities, technical support, and disaster management.

a135.speaker: Kurynin Roman Viktorovich, Deputy Minister of the Ministry of Civil Protection, Emergencies and Disaster Management of the Russian Federation, and Alexey Alsufev, Governor of the Arkhangelsk Region
a135.name: Kurynin Roman Viktorovich
a135.title: Deputy Minister of the Ministry of Civil Protection, Emergencies and Disaster Management of the Russian Federation, and Alexey Alsufev, Governor of the Arkhangelsk Region
a135.speech: Reiterated Russia's commitment to supporting the Somali people through humanitarian assistance and the development of various projects aimed at improving the country's infrastructure and overall wellbeing.

a285.speaker: Constitutional Court of Benin, decision DCC 13-061
a285.name: Constitutional Court of Benin
a285.title: decision DCC 13-061
a285.speech: Examining a citizen's appeal, confirmed Mrs. Lamatou Nassirou as a constitutional judge, writing "that it follows from this provision (article 115) that the appointed member of the Constitutional Court must, in addition to the condition of professional competence, be of good morals and of great probity, and that, unlike magistrates and jurists, for whom at least fifteen years of experience in the exercise of their functions is required, the drafters of 1990 imposed no other criterion for the choice of the figure of great professional reputation to be appointed" ; "professional competence can only be assessed in the light of the appraisals made by hierarchical superiors or by the competent authorities or those empowered to do so; that this appraisal may also be made on the basis of the curriculum vitae, which indicates the training and activities of the prospective member" ; "that she served in several bodies with competence and dedication before being appointed, by decree adopted in the Council of Ministers, Director of Human Resources of the Ministry of the Family and of the Child; that it is therefore established that she fulfils the conditions required to be appointed as a figure of great professional reputation".

a285.speaker: Lamatou Nassirou, constitutional judge nominee and Director of Human Resources at the Ministry of the Family (brief to the Constitutional Court)
a285.name: Lamatou Nassirou
a285.title: constitutional judge nominee and Director of Human Resources at the Ministry of the Family (brief to the Constitutional Court)
a285.speech: "According to the Larousse dictionary, a personality is a person holding a high office. Following the Council of Ministers of 15 November 2007, I was appointed by presidential decree as Director of Human Resources at the Ministry in charge of the Family. This appointment in the Council of Ministers confers on me, under the terms of article 56 cited above, the status of 'Senior Civil Servant' and consequently of a Personality".

a285.speaker: Lamatou Nassirou (brief to the Constitutional Court)
a285.name: Lamatou Nassirou (brief to the Constitutional Court)
a285.speech: "A 'figure of great professional reputation'? I am one without any doubt, as the President of the Republic very rightly appreciated in his sovereign judgment. Indeed, as an official of the Beninese administration, I held the position of Director of Human Resources (DRH) at the Ministry in charge of the family, where I managed the careers of all the staff of that Ministry, represented in every commune of Benin, including those of the four Ministers who succeeded one another at the head of that Ministerial Department" ; says she collaborated on the CLEF Project (Children Learning and Equity Foundation)/USAID.

a285.speaker: Lamatou Nassirou (brief to the Constitutional Court)
a285.name: Lamatou Nassirou (brief to the Constitutional Court)
a285.speech: To justify her appointment as a "sage" at the age of 41, invokes the elections of the baby dictators in Togo (Faure) and in the DRC (Kabila), and compares her appointment at 41 to the election of Barack Obama as a "senator" at the age of 36 ; refers to "a certain wavering public opinion changing according to the individuals who animate it".

a285.speaker: Thomas Boni Yayi, President of the Republic of Benin (response to the appeal, cited in decision DCC 13-061)
a285.name: Thomas Boni Yayi
a285.title: President of the Republic of Benin (response to the appeal, cited in decision DCC 13-061)
a285.speech: Wrote "that the appointment of Madame Lamatou Nassirou was made by virtue of the provisions of article 115 of our Constitution and that the criteria which prevailed in this choice stem from her 'faith in the Republic, one and indivisible, whose institutions must be animated by women and men driven by the ethical and moral values of integrity, transparency, good governance, the obligation of results, accountability and the fight against corruption and impunity'; that he specifies that the appointment of Madame Lamatou Nassirou complies with these requirements, which he considers cardinal and which are apparent through her career, marked by her multiple professional experiences and her demonstrated competences".

a285.speaker: Larousse and Petit Robert dictionaries
a285.name: Larousse and Petit Robert dictionaries
a285.speech: Larousse says a personality is "a person who is known by reason of their functions, their influence"; the Petit Robert says "a person in the public eye, notable for their social situation, their activity".

a285.speaker: CLEF project report (USAID, pages 16-17)
a285.name: CLEF project report (USAID
a285.title: pages 16-17)
a285.speech: Lists the project's key personnel and its Beninese consultants (Agniola Badarou, Rebecca Dossou Gbete, Dr. Lydie Pognon, Dr. Christophe Oku); Mrs. Lamatou's name appears in neither list.

a285.speaker: Charles C Lokonon, political scientist (author)
a285.name: Charles C Lokonon
a285.title: political scientist (author)
a285.speech: Argues that by its decision the Constitutional Court appears to abdicate its right and duty to interpret the constitution, setting the bar lower than the drafters by replacing the requirement of "great professional reputation" with that of "professional competence", and that minimum competence cannot be a sufficient criterion for elevation to the highest institution of the country ; argues that the central role of the Court requires that those appointed be of a superior calibre in their intellectual faculties and their proven contribution to the protection of individual and public liberties, and that any other consideration of gender balance or ethnic origin must be subordinate to that mission.

a411.speaker: Martin McLaughlin, USAID Deputy Mission Director (Mozambique)
a411.name: Martin McLaughlin
a411.title: USAID Deputy Mission Director (Mozambique)
a411.speech: “This new oxygen plant is a physical symbol of what the U.S. and Mozambican partnership can build together,” said Mr. McLaughlin during the handover ceremony. “We have invested more than $94 million in COVID assistance nationwide, including here in Nampula, to build the capacity of health workers and strengthen the health system. We will continue to work together because a healthy, resilient Mozambique leads to a healthy, resilient world.”

a411.speaker: US Agency for International Development (USAID) (press statement)
a411.name: US Agency for International Development (USAID) (press statement)
a411.speech: USAID leads the U.S. Government's international development and disaster assistance through partnerships and investments that save lives, reduce poverty, strengthen democratic governance, and help people emerge from humanitarian crises.

a668.speaker: Renee Demarco, Acting USAID Country Representative in Namibia
a668.name: Renee Demarco
a668.title: Acting USAID Country Representative in Namibia
a668.speech: Says that the donation will assist in reducing the number of young women turning to transactional sex and reducing the cycle of poverty: "One vital component of dreams is called intensive economic strengthening. This intervention empowers young women economically and reduces their vulnerability to HIV infection. Women between the ages of 15 and 24 benefit from financial literacy education, vocational training and job placement, social asset building, and mentorship."

a668.speaker: Emma Kantema-Gaomas, Namibian Deputy Minister of Sports, Youth and National Service
a668.name: Emma Kantema-Gaomas
a668.title: Namibian Deputy Minister of Sports, Youth and National Service
a668.speech: Says the donation will assist in reducing unemployment, uplift the youth in rural areas, and impart skills to young women and adolescents.

a762.speaker: Residents of Kwania and Kole districts
a762.name: Residents of Kwania and Kole districts
a762.speech: Raised concerns about unemployment, poor road infrastructure, and limited access to health services—issues they want the candidate to address once elected president.

a836.speaker: Residents of the areas bordering Kebbi State
a836.name: Residents of the areas bordering Kebbi State
a836.speech: According to the report, lamented the substantial losses they faced, including crops such as maize, yams, cotton, and beans.

a836.speaker: United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation, the World Food Programme, the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security, and other partners (projection)
a836.name: United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation
a836.title: the World Food Programme, the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security, and other partners (projection)
a836.speech: Projected that 33.1 million people across 26 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) will face food and nutrition crisis between June and August next year.

a836.speaker: Daily Trust (this newspaper's own reporting)
a836.name: Daily Trust (this newspaper's own reporting)
a836.speech: Has reported several times that farmers in Kaduna, Katsina, Zamfara, Sokoto, and other northern states have had to pay bandits before being allowed to access their farms for planting, and that during harvest some of these farmers again had to pay bandits before being permitted to take their produce home.

a836.speaker: Bola Ahmed Tinubu, President of Nigeria
a836.name: Bola Ahmed Tinubu
a836.title: President of Nigeria
a836.speech: Addressed this issue at the G-20 Summit in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, stating, "I am from Nigeria, and it is better to give you the true picture of what is going on in Africa. We have terrorism challenges - insecurity challenges that are preventing farmers from even going to their farms."

a836.speaker: Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF) and other respected Nigerians and groups
a836.name: Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF) and other respected Nigerians and groups
a836.speech: Argue that the growing food crisis should be addressed through both short-term and long-term measures, including imports where necessary.

a856.speaker: Royal Moroccan Football Federation
a856.name: Royal Moroccan Football Federation
a856.speech: Had announced the venues of the sporting fixtures for CAN 2025.

a856.speaker: "Hotel Chain Development Pipeline" report, produced by W Hospitality Group
a856.name: "Hotel Chain Development Pipeline" report
a856.title: produced by W Hospitality Group
a856.speech: According to the latest report, Morocco has positioned itself in 3rd place in the top 10 of the hotel industry in Africa, with 46 establishments of different sizes.

a856.speaker: Fatim-Zahra Ammor, Moroccan Minister of Tourism, Handicrafts and the Social Economy
a856.name: Fatim-Zahra Ammor
a856.title: Moroccan Minister of Tourism, Handicrafts and the Social Economy
a856.speech: Recently announced figures showing the Moroccan tourism sector had an exceptional year in 2024, with nearly 16 million tourist arrivals recorded by the end of November, growth of 20%, i.e. 2.6 million additional visitors compared with the same period in 2023.

a936.speaker: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula, Minister of Health and Social Services of Namibia
a936.name: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula
a936.title: Minister of Health and Social Services of Namibia
a936.speech: Says the opening of the Oroutumba community health post strengthens the public health care system and brings services closer to the people: “This means that one does not need to sell goats, cows, or other properties in order to access or receive health care services. This is what the launch of the community health post signifies and demonstrates.”

a936.speaker: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula, Minister of Health and Social Services of Namibia
a936.name: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula
a936.title: Minister of Health and Social Services of Namibia
a936.speech: “In fact, it is part and parcel of the Namibian government's plan that was approved by the cabinet to mobilise resources in order to strengthen the public health system. The plan is costing more than N$16 billion and will be implemented over a period of 5 years.”

a936.speaker: US Ambassador to Namibia (represented at the event)
a936.name: US Ambassador to Namibia (represented at the event)
a936.speech: According to the US Ambassador to Namibia, the US government has so far assisted Namibia in establishing 12 community health posts in seven regions, and it has also supported the country's community health workers programme: “PEPFAR and the global fund have been collaborating with the ministry of health in these efforts to bring health care services to remote communities. Community health posts are designed to bring quality health care services to the Namibian people and will hopefully encourage an increase in health-seeking behaviour among members of the community.”

a1109.speaker: Hon Ifunanya Nwanegwo, Chairman, Mbaitoli LGA, Imo state (Facebook post)
a1109.name: Hon Ifunanya Nwanegwo
a1109.title: Chairman, Mbaitoli LGA, Imo state (Facebook post)
a1109.speech: In the post, she was appreciating the Director General of the Department of State Services (DSS), Mr Oluwatosin Adeola Ajayi, for empowering ten people in the LGA to help them boost their small businesses.

a1109.speaker: One of Oluwatosin Adeola Ajayi's university classmates
a1109.name: One of Oluwatosin Adeola Ajayi's university classmates
a1109.speech: "He is led by principles of humanity, not of politics, nor religion nor tribe or any sentiment whatsoever," said one of his university classmates.

a1109.speaker: A now retired deputy director of the Department of State Services
a1109.name: A now retired deputy director of the Department of State Services
a1109.speech: Offered that while serving in Bauchi state, Ajayi renovated a mosque at Tafewa-Balewa, rebuilt the Church of Christ in Nations (COCIN) which was in near ruins, and renovated the Evangelical Church of West Africa (ECWA) church there.

a1109.speaker: A retired director of the Department of State Services
a1109.name: A retired director of the Department of State Services
a1109.speech: Noted that one of the driving forces of the DSS boss is his belief that any intelligence service without human asset will be struggling as, according to the spy chief, human intelligence aka HUMINT is more effective, and that he reportedly believes that the collection of information from human sources through interpersonal contact is very effective.

a1109.speaker: Serving and retired personnel of the DSS
a1109.name: Serving and retired personnel of the DSS
a1109.speech: Most serving and retired personnel of the DSS the writer interacted with say they've never had it so good — better remunerated, personnel issues prioritized, families of personnel lost in the line of duty adequately compensated, wives and relatives of inactive personnel empowered, and personnel hopeful for a better future in the Service.

a1311.speaker: Mahamoud Omar Guelleh, Director General of ANEFIP (Djibouti's National Agency for Employment, Training and Professional Integration)
a1311.name: Mahamoud Omar Guelleh
a1311.title: Director General of ANEFIP (Djibouti's National Agency for Employment, Training and Professional Integration)
a1311.speech: At the certificate award ceremony, encouraged jobseekers to seize every opportunity to gain experience in the world of work, even if it is only a small amount of experience, and to register with ANEFIP's agencies.

a1311.speaker: Laura Dillon-Binkley, head of the PED (Djiboutian Workforce Employability) project
a1311.name: Laura Dillon-Binkley
a1311.title: head of the PED (Djiboutian Workforce Employability) project
a1311.speech: Urged them to move forward and to take their own initiatives in searching for work.

a1311.speaker: Moussa Abdillahi, USAID representative
a1311.name: Moussa Abdillahi
a1311.title: USAID representative
a1311.speech: Congratulated the participants on having completed the training and wished them good luck.

a1311.speaker: A female participant from the Gabode centre (anonymous)
a1311.name: A female participant from the Gabode centre (anonymous)
a1311.speech: Said that “to go out into the field you have to be armed. And for me, this training is my weapon.”

a1311.speaker: A participant from the Tadjourah region (anonymous)
a1311.name: A participant from the Tadjourah region (anonymous)
a1311.speech: Shared that “before the training, I blamed everyone else for my situation. Now I am convinced that I am the sole master of my own future.”

a1625.speaker: Christopher Kalokoala, REMM Associates, Kagera
a1625.name: Christopher Kalokoala
a1625.title: REMM Associates, Kagera
a1625.speech: Emphasised that enhancing international tax cooperation is a critical strategy; noted that Tanzania, like many developing countries, suffers significant revenue losses due to tax evasion, often linked to assets held abroad or income generated by multinational corporations, and explained these losses can be addressed through stronger mechanisms for international collaboration in tax matters; further highlighted that improving international tax cooperation would enable Tanzania to achieve more accurate and comprehensive reporting of foreign-sourced incomes earned by its residents, boosting transparency, promoting a fairer distribution of tax responsibilities and curbing the offshore concealment of wealth.

a1625.speaker: Hindustan Times
a1625.name: Hindustan Times
a1625.speech: According to it, India's Automatic Exchange of Information (AEOI) initiative has led to the identification of approximately 21.8bn Euro in additional revenue from 2009 to 2023, underscoring its effectiveness in enhancing tax compliance and transparency across several countries.

a1625.speaker: Reports by the South African Revenue Service and the OECD
a1625.name: Reports by the South African Revenue Service and the OECD
a1625.speech: Detail that South Africa and other African nations have collectively recovered over 1.69 billion Euros in additional revenue from compliance initiatives, such as voluntary disclosure programmes and offshore income investigations, underscoring the financial benefits of committed international tax cooperation and adherence to global transparency standards.

a1625.speaker: Florida James, financial analyst with the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) Tanzania country office
a1625.name: Florida James
a1625.title: financial analyst with the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) Tanzania country office
a1625.speech: Underscored the transformative potential of introducing taxpayer advocacy services to reform Tanzania's personal tax system; drawing from the successful model of the US Taxpayer Advocate Service (TAS), she highlighted how such services can demystify complex tax processes, alleviating frustrations and challenges faced by taxpayers; according to her, taxpayer advocacy plays a pivotal role in guiding individuals through the system, helping them understand their rights and responsibilities, resolving disputes efficiently and fostering effective communication between taxpayers and tax authorities. She elaborated with examples of TAS's impactful interventions - a taxpayer who received an Offset Bypass Refund to cover urgent medical travel expenses, and a case where TAS expedited the processing of amended tax returns to correct a significant tax liability - explaining that these illustrate how taxpayer advocacy services could foster trust, improve compliance, and create a more inclusive tax environment in Tanzania.

a1625.speaker: Taxpayer Advocate Service (TAS) annual reports
a1625.name: Taxpayer Advocate Service (TAS) annual reports
a1625.speech: Highlight that the service resolves hundreds of thousands of taxpayers' issues each year, with a high success rate in reducing taxpayers' liabilities and navigating complex disputes.

a1625.speaker: Rebecca Lianga, Managing Partner at Rebbla Attorneys, Dar es Salaam
a1625.name: Rebecca Lianga
a1625.title: Managing Partner at Rebbla Attorneys, Dar es Salaam
a1625.speech: Highlighted the urgency of modernising tax laws to address digital transactions; stressed that updating these laws is essential to safeguarding the tax base amid ongoing economic transformation; according to her, effectively capturing revenue from digital platforms and e-commerce not only prevents tax base erosion but also fosters a fairer and more sustainable taxation framework, aligning with the realities of an increasingly digitalised economy.

a1625.speaker: Research on the European Union's One-Stop-Shop (OSS) system (cited)
a1625.name: Research on the European Union's One-Stop-Shop (OSS) system (cited)
a1625.speech: Cites the success of the EU's One-Stop-Shop system, a cornerstone of the VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) initiative, which has streamlined VAT processes for cross-border transactions, with projections of increasing VAT revenues by up to 18 billion Euros annually, including 11 billion Euros from anti-fraud measures.

a1625.speaker: Deogratius Diu, PricewaterhouseCoopers
a1625.name: Deogratius Diu
a1625.title: PricewaterhouseCoopers
a1625.speech: Pointed to Australia's introduction of GST on digital services provided by non-residents in 2017, which has significantly boosted tax revenues, generating an estimated 350 million AUD annually.

a1625.speaker: Phillipina Assenga, lead accountant for Tanzania's 50bn/- "Maji Bombani" project in Rukwa
a1625.name: Phillipina Assenga
a1625.title: lead accountant for Tanzania's 50bn/- "Maji Bombani" project in Rukwa
a1625.speech: Highlighted research demonstrating how African nations are successfully adapting VAT policies to tax digital transactions; noted that countries like Nigeria, Ghana and Kenya are leveraging existing legal frameworks to streamline administration and effectively capture revenue from the rapidly expanding digital economy.

a1625.speaker: Victor Tesha, Isale Group, Vice President of the Tanzania Small Miners Association and Board Chairman of the Copyright Society of Tanzania
a1625.name: Victor Tesha
a1625.title: Isale Group, Vice President of the Tanzania Small Miners Association and Board Chairman of the Copyright Society of Tanzania
a1625.speech: Underlined the importance of tailoring tax automation in Tanzania to the country's rural demographics and varying levels of digital literacy; explained that mobile-friendly tax platforms integrated with mobile money services like M-Pesa could make tax registration, filing and payment far more accessible to rural communities; stressed the need for education campaigns in local languages and decentralised digital kiosks equipped with internet access and trained staff; suggested linking tax accounts to the National ID system to streamline processes and improve compliance, while SMS and USSD technologies could bridge accessibility gaps; said leveraging data analytics and AI tools to identify untapped taxpayer segments and improve enforcement would further strengthen the system; and advocated for expanding digital infrastructure through partnerships with telecom providers and rolling out pilot programmes, concluding that these initiatives could significantly broaden Tanzania's taxpayer base, enhance compliance and drive sustainable economic growth.

a1625.speaker: Research on South Korea's e-tax system (cited)
a1625.name: Research on South Korea's e-tax system (cited)
a1625.speech: Examines Korea's National Tax Service transition to a comprehensive electronic tax system, finding that by 2020 over 96 per cent of corporate taxpayers and 95 per cent of individual taxpayers were filing electronically, that tax revenue rose from 110 billion US dollars in 2000 to over 230 billion US dollars by 2015, and that the cost of collecting taxes dropped from 0.91 US dollars per 100 US dollars collected in 2000 to just 0.45 US dollars by 2015.

a1647.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of Mozambique
a1647.name: Daniel Chapo
a1647.title: President of Mozambique
a1647.speech: Expressed today his commitment to Public-Private Dialogue, with a view to accelerating reforms and improving the business environment in the country ; expressed the Government's openness to collaborating with the private sector on the reform agenda in order to attract investment, increase national production and boost exports ; urged the CTA to present concrete reform proposals in line with the difficulties they face in their day-to-day activities.

a1647.speaker: Álvaro Massinga, President of the Confederation of Economic Associations (CTA)
a1647.name: Álvaro Massinga
a1647.title: President of the Confederation of Economic Associations (CTA)
a1647.speech: Said the work agenda of the recently formed team is anchored in a Manifesto structured around five strategic areas, namely the Promotion of Structural Economic Reforms; Promotion of Associative and Institutional Development; Active Participation of the Private Sector in Infrastructure and Public Services; and Human Capital Development and Promotion of Local Content ; also announced that the Business Environment Monitoring Council (CEMAN), to be led by the Prime Minister, will be held this month, and the Private Sector Conference (CASP) between October and November, an event traditionally chaired by the Head of State.

a1882.speaker: Thompson, USAID South Sudan Mission Director
a1882.name: Thompson
a1882.title: USAID South Sudan Mission Director
a1882.speech: emphasized the critical need for free and fair elections in South Sudan to ensure that leaders are accountable to the people: “For democracy to thrive, this country needs free and fair elections to elect leaders who will be accountable to the people of South Sudan.”

a1882.speaker: Thompson, USAID South Sudan Mission Director
a1882.name: Thompson
a1882.title: USAID South Sudan Mission Director
a1882.speech: stressed that South Sudan is rich in resources which, if managed transparently and effectively, could support the country’s electoral process without relying on external assistance: “This country has resources that, when used transparently and appropriately, could support elections without looking for external support.”

a1882.speaker: Thompson, USAID South Sudan Mission Director
a1882.name: Thompson
a1882.title: USAID South Sudan Mission Director
a1882.speech: emphasized that while USAID is considering supporting South Sudan’s 2026 elections, the transitional government must show tangible progress toward ensuring free and fair elections and demonstrate real efforts in implementing reforms: “We want to see demonstrable evidence that the transitional government is making real efforts and progress toward that goal.”

a1882.speaker: Thompson, USAID South Sudan Mission Director
a1882.name: Thompson
a1882.title: USAID South Sudan Mission Director
a1882.speech: called on South Sudanese leaders to take ownership of the country’s challenges, particularly in responding to emergencies, improving disaster preparedness, and ensuring that public funds are used transparently: “The transitional government has a critical role in responding to emergencies by mobilizing resources, improving disaster preparedness, and ensuring that public funds are used transparently.” ; “South Sudanese leaders must also create the conditions that enable effective international support by fostering stability and accountability.”

a1955.speaker: Mahatma Gandhi
a1955.name: Mahatma Gandhi
a1955.speech: Suggested that we are to judge the greatness of a nation by the way its animals are treated.

a1955.speaker: Gwede Mantashe, ANC secretary general
a1955.name: Gwede Mantashe
a1955.title: ANC secretary general
a1955.speech: Suggested, after the last violent spasm earlier this year, that one solution would be to set up “refugee camps so that we can document people”.

a1955.speaker: NGOs working with refugees and asylum seekers to South Africa
a1955.name: NGOs working with refugees and asylum seekers to South Africa
a1955.speech: Have for years reported on the endemic corruption in the system.

a1955.speaker: Public Protector (2004 report)
a1955.name: Public Protector (2004 report)
a1955.speech: Published a report in 2004 on unlawful conduct at the Braamfontein refugee reception office.

a1955.speaker: US State Department (annual country reports, 2009-2013)
a1955.name: US State Department (annual country reports
a1955.speech: Have consistently flagged corruption in annual country reports, stating, “although the department of home affairs (DHA) had anti-corruption programmes in place and punished officials or contracted security officers found to be accepting bribes, NGOs and asylum applicants continued to report that immigration authorities sought bribes from those seeking permits to remain in the country, particularly in cases where applicants allowed their documents to expire”.

a1955.speaker: Roni Amit, author of the report ‘Queue Here For Corruption – Measuring Irregularities in South Africa’s Asylum System’
a1955.name: Roni Amit
a1955.title: author of the report ‘Queue Here For Corruption – Measuring Irregularities in South Africa’s Asylum System’
a1955.speech: Writes: “When LHR expressed its concerns over the way the operation was being managed, officers from the counter-corruption unit criticised the organisation for forcing its client to withdraw from the operation. The officers again contacted the client directly and threatened to arrest her for not co-operating. In addition, they suggested completing the operation with counterfeit notes, promising to get her released if she was arrested on counterfeiting charges” ; “Fearing that this would subject the client to intimidation at the RRO, LHR declined to provide this information. Subsequently, the new centre manager at Marabastad arranged for the client to undergo another status determination interview and she was granted refugee status.”

a1955.speaker: Roni Amit, author of the report
a1955.name: Roni Amit
a1955.title: author of the report
a1955.speech: Writes that the assessment revealed “significant levels of corruption involving multiple actors, occurring at all stages of the asylum process, and continuing even after an individual had obtained refugee status. Results varied by office, but overall almost one-third of respondents experienced corruption at an RRO. The Marabastad RRO in Pretoria showed the highest levels of corruption” ; reports that the presence of corruption is significant “for its effects on the ability of individuals to access protection; on the integrity of a system that is an integral part of South Africa’s constitutional and international obligations; and on the incentive structures within and rational functioning of the public service. Continued corruption risks producing a system where the behaviour of public officials is removed from legal guarantees and the principles of equality, fairness, and accountability”.

a1955.speaker: Roni Amit, author of the report
a1955.name: Roni Amit
a1955.title: author of the report
a1955.speech: Writes that even as government continued to point to the “scourge” of economic migrants abusing the asylum system, it did little to combat the corruption that enables individuals without protection needs to claim asylum while denying this very protection to the system’s intended beneficiaries.

a1955.speaker: Roni Amit, author of the report
a1955.name: Roni Amit
a1955.title: author of the report
a1955.speech: Said in an interview yesterday that she had attempted to engage with the department of home affairs with regard to the report but until now no response had been forthcoming.

a1955.speaker: Report ‘Queue Here For Corruption’ (African Centre for Migration and Society and Lawyers for Human Rights), based on a survey of 928 asylum seekers and refugees
a1955.name: Report ‘Queue Here For Corruption’ (African Centre for Migration and Society and Lawyers for Human Rights)
a1955.title: based on a survey of 928 asylum seekers and refugees
a1955.speech: Found that several factors had contributed to the prevalence of corruption in the country’s refugee reception offices, foremost the department of home affairs’ failure to respond to high levels of demand that quickly exceeded the capacity of a system designed around individualised decision-making, and that the decision to close three refugee reception offices has contributed to these problems; it reported that 13% of respondents paid border officials, 20% overall (51% at Marabastad) were harassed for bribes in queues, 13% (30% at Marabastad) were denied access to offices without paying a bribe, 12% (24% at Marabastad) had paid at least once to renew asylum permits, and 20% (47% at Marabastad) were asked for money to resolve an issue speedily.

a1955.speaker: Report ‘Queue Here For Corruption’
a1955.name: Report ‘Queue Here For Corruption’
a1955.speech: States: “It is precisely those migrants whose entry the government is seeking to control who can undermine these controls by engaging with corrupt officials. At the same time, individuals with valid protection needs may be denied protection because they are either unwilling or unable to engage with these same officials” ; “These conditions create multiple opportunities for corruption. Additional factors provide further incentives: individuals must generally make multiple visits to a refugee reception office to address a single issue; they remain in the system for several years, necessitating even more visits; and they receive legally problematic status determination decisions that require appeals. Rather than address the factors contributing to corruption, the DHA has adopted a reactive approach in which it responds to individual allegations of corruption; it has, thus far, failed to initiate more far-reaching investigations or reforms of the asylum system” ; “In order to address the prevalence of corruption, the department of home affairs (DHA) and other stakeholders must recognise that it pervades all stages of the asylum process, that it occurs at multiple sites, and that it is a continuing phenomenon that is not confined to isolated individuals or incidents.” The report makes various recommendations to the DHA, to parliament and the committee for home affairs, the public protector and South African Human Rights Commission, the National Prosecuting Authority and the South African Police Services, including professionalising the status determination process and requiring refugee status determination officers to provide specific reasons for rejections and approvals.

a1955.speaker: Department of Home Affairs (preliminary figures for the 2013 calendar year)
a1955.name: Department of Home Affairs (preliminary figures for the 2013 calendar year)
a1955.speech: Preliminary figures released by the DHA for the 2013 calendar year indicate that applicants from Burundi and Somalia had decreased significantly, with the highest numbers of asylum applicants in 2013 from Zimbabwe, Nigeria, the DRC, and Ethiopia.

a1955.speaker: Lawyers for Human Rights (LHR)
a1955.name: Lawyers for Human Rights (LHR)
a1955.speech: Expressed its concerns over the way the sting operation was being managed and declined to provide the complainant’s contact details, fearing that this would subject the client to intimidation at the refugee reception office.

a1955.speaker: Counter-corruption unit of the Department of Home Affairs
a1955.name: Counter-corruption unit of the Department of Home Affairs
a1955.speech: A week after agreeing to set up the sting operation, contacted LHR asking whether the organisation or the woman who had made the complaint would be able to provide a portion of the R2,500 bribe.

a1955.speaker: Department of Home Affairs
a1955.name: Department of Home Affairs
a1955.speech: Has not responded to the report; Amit said no response had been forthcoming from the department.

a2036.speaker: Organisers of the conference (Autorité nationale de lutte contre la corruption)
a2036.name: Organisers of the conference (Autorité nationale de lutte contre la corruption)
a2036.speech: According to the organisers, the overall objective of the conference is to prompt broader reflection among the actors involved in the fight against transnational organised crime and corruption in Benin with a view to reinvigorating the fight against these two phenomena; specifically, to share with participants the content of the special study on transnational organised crime (TOC) and corruption, particularly its arms-trafficking dimension, to share the content of the second quarterly evaluation of judicial proceedings relating to TOC and corruption cases with emphasis on arms trafficking, to share the cross-cutting experience of professionals fighting transnational organised crime in Benin at institutional and jurisdictional levels, and finally to gather recommendations for a more effective fight against corruption and transnational organised crime.

a2036.speaker: Guy Ogoubiyi, President of the Autorité nationale de lutte contre la corruption (ANLC)
a2036.name: Guy Ogoubiyi
a2036.title: President of the Autorité nationale de lutte contre la corruption (ANLC)
a2036.speech: In his remarks at the opening of proceedings, first recalled the "Ayifa" project, which he said falls within the framework of Benin's West African Security Cooperation Initiative Programme launched by the government. He stressed that the combination of transnational organised crime (TOC) and corruption and of arms trafficking linked to organised armed robberies in Benin calls for reflection in view of the security situation in the West African sub-region in general and Benin's geographical position in particular. He also expressed the hope that the recommendations would be of high quality so as to improve the institutional and regulatory framework needed to begin rolling back transnational organised crime and corruption in Benin.

a2036.speaker: Yikee Chu Adjé, representative of USAID-Benin
a2036.name: Yikee Chu Adjé
a2036.title: representative of USAID-Benin
a2036.speech: Returned to the importance of the theme, which she described as topical, calling it a worrying phenomenon that deserves an appropriate response and the support of the international community. "The phenomenon deserves sustained attention from the government and requires a global reflection on the situation in order to assess the institutional framework in place and counter the phenomenon." ; "The security of citizens and of economic activity is a guarantee of development."

a2135.speaker: Augusta Maita, Executive Director of the Millennium Challenge Account Mozambique
a2135.name: Augusta Maita
a2135.title: Executive Director of the Millennium Challenge Account Mozambique
a2135.speech: Released the information on Saturday in Quelimane, following a meeting with project implementation partners, that the government may invest US$200 million (12 billion meticais) from the Millennium Challenge Account on the construction of a new Mocuba Ring Road and alternative bridge over the Licungo river in Zambezia, with construction beginning in September next year and possibly lasting five years. ; Says that public consultations and technical studies are underway to ensure the viability of the project.

a2135.speaker: Cristina Mafumo, Secretary of State for Zambezia
a2135.name: Cristina Mafumo
a2135.title: Secretary of State for Zambezia
a2135.speech: Said that the funding would boost economic growth in the country.

a2142.speaker: Elias Magosi, Executive Secretary of the Southern African Development Community (SADC)
a2142.name: Elias Magosi
a2142.title: Executive Secretary of the Southern African Development Community (SADC)
a2142.speech: Called on member states to reduce their dependence on foreign aid and to promote regional self-reliance, citing rising geopolitical tensions, trade disruptions and the sharp decline in external funding. Speaking on Tuesday at the opening of the SADC Council of Ministers meeting in Madagascar, he said that the current global context, marked by tariff increases and shifting alliances, underscores the urgency for the region to invest in its own resilience: "It is becoming increasingly clear to all of us that our chances are better when we rely more on our own resources than on foreign aid, over which we have absolutely no control."

a2142.speaker: Elias Magosi, Executive Secretary of the Southern African Development Community (SADC)
a2142.name: Elias Magosi
a2142.title: Executive Secretary of the Southern African Development Community (SADC)
a2142.speech: Urged governments to step up intra-regional trade, remove obstacles and invest in infrastructure that accelerates integration; he also called for moving away from exporting raw materials, stressing that manufacturing contributes only 11% of SADC's gross domestic product, well below the target of 30% by 2030.

a2142.speaker: 24th meeting of the SADC Committee of Ministers of Trade, Harare (resolutions)
a2142.name: 24th meeting of the SADC Committee of Ministers of Trade
a2142.title: Harare (resolutions)
a2142.speech: Ministers committed to boosting industrialisation, value addition and regional trade in goods and services.

a2193.speaker: European Parliament (resolution of May 8, 2025)
a2193.name: European Parliament (resolution of May 8
a2193.speech: Passed a resolution expressing concern over the arrest and prosecution of CHADEMA national chairperson, Tundu Lissu; the resolution called for his "immediate and unconditional" release, accusing the Tanzanian government of politically motivated repression and warning of consequences for European Union (EU) – Tanzania relations if what it termed "democratic backsliding" persists.

a2193.speaker: Tanzania's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and East African Cooperation
a2193.name: Tanzania's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and East African Cooperation
a2193.speech: Described the resolution as based on "incomplete or partisan information" and as "an inappropriate interference in the country's internal affairs."

a2193.speaker: United Nations Charter, Article 2(7)
a2193.name: United Nations Charter
a2193.title: Article 2(7)
a2193.speech: Explicitly protects the sovereignty of states, prohibiting UN intervention in matters essentially within domestic jurisdiction.

a2201.speaker: Cameron Hudson, senior fellow in the Africa Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies
a2201.name: Cameron Hudson
a2201.title: senior fellow in the Africa Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies
a2201.speech: Explains that this shift in momentum is the first opportunity for the Trump administration to use its leverage with regional and Gulf state allies to help press for a ceasefire.

a2201.speaker: Cameron Hudson, senior fellow in the Africa Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies
a2201.name: Cameron Hudson
a2201.title: senior fellow in the Africa Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies
a2201.speech: On the current status of the war: "The war in Sudan is approaching its two-year anniversary next month and is entering a new though perhaps equally dangerous phase." Said Sudan's army has continued its momentum-shifting offensive, retaking the presidential palace, while humanitarian conditions continue to worsen with more than 30 million people in need of humanitarian assistance and 13 million displaced; famine warnings are in place for 5 of Sudan's 18 states, and "international humanitarian assistance is both struggling to get through and in insufficient supply, increasing the likelihood of widespread starvation deaths in 2025." Noted last year's UN $4 billion appeal for Sudan was only 50 percent met and this year the demand has increased an additional 50 percent to $6 billion, "suggesting that the assistance gap is only likely to grow unless international efforts to respond are increased."

a2201.speaker: Cameron Hudson, senior fellow in the Africa Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies
a2201.name: Cameron Hudson
a2201.title: senior fellow in the Africa Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies
a2201.speech: On the significance of the army reclaiming the Republican Palace: said it is "both a tactical and strategic victory over the RSF militia," though the RSF still controls much of the city's southern suburbs; said the victory brings new pressure on the army to restore essential services like water and electricity, deliver food aid and open transport routes, and that the army has given indications it could announce the appointment of a new technocratic, civilian transitional government, which "properly empowered" could help avert the impending famine the capital faces.

a2201.speaker: Cameron Hudson, senior fellow in the Africa Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies
a2201.name: Cameron Hudson
a2201.title: senior fellow in the Africa Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies
a2201.speech: On what is likely to come next: said the momentum shift has been driven by the SAF's aggressive rearmament and recruitment, including TB2 drones from Turkey and fighter jets and heavy armaments from China and Russia, and reliance on Islamist militias backed by the former Bashir regime; said the RSF is likely to fall back to Darfur and attempt to complete its siege of El Fasher, which "would have potentially catastrophic humanitarian consequences for the more than 1 million internally displaced sheltering in camps around the city," and that Sudan could face "a Libya-like scenario with two separate governments vying for recognition and credibility."

a2201.speaker: Cameron Hudson, senior fellow in the Africa Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies
a2201.name: Cameron Hudson
a2201.title: senior fellow in the Africa Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies
a2201.speech: On prospects for peace: said neither side "has given any suggestion that they are interested in a negotiated settlement," but "now is perhaps the best moment in nearly two years of fighting to push the parties and their backers to de-escalate"; criticised international attention being captured by Gaza and Ukraine, said the UN and African Union have been "heavily criticised for their mostly hands-off approach," and said an upcoming donor conference in London presents an opportunity "but only if it includes the parties to the conflict who are not presently invited."

a2201.speaker: Cameron Hudson, senior fellow in the Africa Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies
a2201.name: Cameron Hudson
a2201.title: senior fellow in the Africa Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies
a2201.speech: On US policy: said the Trump administration "has thus far given little indication as to which way it will lean in Sudan's conflict"; said Rubio's rejection of the RSF's parallel government suggests a break with Biden administration policy, and that "Washington would be well advised to rebuild its ties to the army and use its relationships with important Gulf actors to finally begin to advance a fragile peace process in Sudan."

a2201.speaker: Sudanese army officials
a2201.name: Sudanese army officials
a2201.speech: Have been promising civilians a swift return to their homes and a chance to start rebuilding their lives once Khartoum was retaken.

a2201.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a2201.name: Marco Rubio
a2201.title: US Secretary of State
a2201.speech: In his Senate confirmation hearing last month, suggested he would take a hard line on the United Arab Emirates' long-running financial and military support to the RSF.

a2201.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a2201.name: Marco Rubio
a2201.title: US Secretary of State
a2201.speech: Made a statement in rejection of the RSF's announcement of a competing government and constitutional document earlier this month, denying the RSF much-needed legitimacy and implicitly acknowledging the army's constitutional role.

a2201.speaker: Rapid Support Forces (RSF)
a2201.name: Rapid Support Forces (RSF)
a2201.speech: Declared last month its own parallel government, announcing a competing government and constitutional document.

a2397.speaker: Health officials (Somalia)
a2397.name: Health officials (Somalia)
a2397.speech: Warning that vaccine shortages, donor funding cuts, and systemic weaknesses have created one of the country’s most dangerous public health crises in years.

a2397.speaker: Ministry of Health (Somalia)
a2397.name: Ministry of Health (Somalia)
a2397.speech: Said more than 1,600 cases and 87 deaths have been reported so far in 2025, nearly double last year’s total.

a2397.speaker: Doctors at De Martino Public Hospital, Mogadishu
a2397.name: Doctors at De Martino Public Hospital
a2397.title: Mogadishu
a2397.speech: Documented a 914 percent increase in cases year-over-year, with deaths tripling from 13 in 2024 to 42 in 2025.

a2397.speaker: Deka Mohamed Ali, displaced mother who fled fighting in central Somalia
a2397.name: Deka Mohamed Ali
a2397.title: displaced mother who fled fighting in central Somalia
a2397.speech: Said that all four of her children contracted diphtheria after arriving in Mogadishu; her eight-year-old son died and two toddlers remain hospitalized. “My children got sick and I just stayed at home because I did not know it was diphtheria,” she told Reuters.

a2397.speaker: Ali Haji Adam, Somali Health Minister
a2397.name: Ali Haji Adam
a2397.title: Somali Health Minister
a2397.speech: Acknowledged that Somalia has struggled to procure vaccines amid a global shortage.

a2397.speaker: Doctors Without Borders (MSF)
a2397.name: Doctors Without Borders (MSF)
a2397.speech: Warned that basic supplies, including the diphtheria antitoxin, have already been exhausted in some hospitals.

a2397.speaker: Frida Athanassiadis, MSF medical coordinator
a2397.name: Frida Athanassiadis
a2397.title: MSF medical coordinator
a2397.speech: “Low vaccination coverage, vaccine hesitancy, and poor living conditions are driving the spread.”

a2397.speaker: Aid agencies
a2397.name: Aid agencies
a2397.speech: Say the outbreak underscores long-standing gaps in Somalia’s health system, where only 4.8 percent of the national budget was allocated to health last year.

a2397.speaker: Save the Children
a2397.name: Save the Children
a2397.speech: Noted that since April, cases of measles, diphtheria, cholera, whooping cough, and severe respiratory infections have more than doubled across the country.

a2397.speaker: Public health experts
a2397.name: Public health experts
a2397.speech: Warn that without urgent, coordinated action, Somalia risks an even wider epidemic.

a2397.speaker: Dr. Abdulrazaq Yusuf Ahmed, director of De Martino Hospital
a2397.name: Dr. Abdulrazaq Yusuf Ahmed
a2397.title: director of De Martino Hospital
a2397.speech: “Timely data saves lives.” ; “What we now need is unified leadership and rapid response”.

a2651.speaker: Tony Cheng, Al Jazeera correspondent reporting from Ho Chi Minh City
a2651.name: Tony Cheng
a2651.title: Al Jazeera correspondent reporting from Ho Chi Minh City
a2651.speech: Said thousands of people stayed in the streets overnight to get the best vantage point for the parade, which was “a day of sombre reflection but also a day of celebration”.

a2651.speaker: Tran Van Truong, 75-year-old Vietnamese war veteran
a2651.name: Tran Van Truong
a2651.title: 75-year-old Vietnamese war veteran
a2651.speech: “I am proud of having contributed to liberating the south,” said 75-year-old veteran Tran Van Truong who had travelled – dressed in full military uniform – from the capital, Hanoi, to see the parade. ; “But what’s gone is gone, I have no hatred for those from the other side of the battle,” Truong told the AFP news agency. “We should join hands to celebrate the end of the war.”

a2651.speaker: Vietnamese state media
a2651.name: Vietnamese state media
a2651.speech: More than 300,000 Chinese soldiers were involved in the bloody conflict, according to state media, providing crucial anti-aircraft defence support and helping with logistics and supplies.

a2651.speaker: Zach Abuza, professor at the National War College in Washington focusing on Southeast Asian politics
a2651.name: Zach Abuza
a2651.title: professor at the National War College in Washington focusing on Southeast Asian politics
a2651.speech: “I think Hanoi is signalling to China that they recognise China’s historical contribution,” said Zach Abuza. “It’s also another way for them to signal: ‘Don’t think our foreign policy is lurching towards the Americans.’”

a2669.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of France
a2669.name: Emmanuel Macron
a2669.title: President of France
a2669.speech: Described Donald Trump's criticism of him as "incidents": "It doesn't move me because I know him and we have a long-standing relationship." ; "He has extremely friendly words but he wanted to reintroduce ambiguity into his position, so he said he was not going to discuss a ceasefire (in Iran)."

a2669.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of France
a2669.name: Emmanuel Macron
a2669.title: President of France
a2669.speech: Had stated on Monday 16 June that his American counterpart's departure from the G7 was linked to "an offer that was made (to the United States) of a meeting and exchange" with the Iranians against a backdrop of an imminent ceasefire.

a2669.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a2669.name: Donald Trump
a2669.title: President of the United States
a2669.speech: Denied Macron's remarks, criticising his counterpart: "Wrong! He has no idea why I am now on my way to Washington, but it certainly has nothing to do with a ceasefire. It's much bigger than that." ; "Whether intentionally or not, Emmanuel never understands anything."

a2669.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of France
a2669.name: Emmanuel Macron
a2669.title: President of France
a2669.speech: "In the grave moment we are living through, I think my role is not to comment on remarks here and there. It is to explain what we want, what useful things we can do and to recall the priorities." ; recalled his "clear" positions on the situation in the Middle East: "an immediate ceasefire in Gaza, the release of all hostages, the resumption of humanitarian aid, the resumption of a political process which is the only future for Gaza", as well as a "ceasefire as soon as possible in Iran and a resumption of discussions".

a2669.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a2669.name: Donald Trump
a2669.title: President of the United States
a2669.speech: Said he wanted a "real end" to the conflict between Iran and Israel, and not a simple ceasefire ; also stated that the United States does not intend to kill the Iranian supreme leader, Ayatollah Khamenei, "for the moment".

a2669.speaker: US government
a2669.name: US government
a2669.speech: Assured that the posture of American forces in the region remained "defensive".

a2669.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of France
a2669.name: Emmanuel Macron
a2669.title: President of France
a2669.speech: "I am not responsible for the changes of mind of the American administration." ; According to him, a change of regime in Iran through war would be synonymous with "chaos".

a2669.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of France
a2669.name: Emmanuel Macron
a2669.title: President of France
a2669.speech: Estimated on Tuesday on the sidelines of the G7 that "the United States is needed to bring everyone back around the negotiating table" in the conflict between Iran and Israel.

a2669.speaker: Israel (Israeli military)
a2669.name: Israel (Israeli military)
a2669.speech: Said it had targeted military sites in Iran in new air strikes, to which Tehran responded with missile fire.

a2978.speaker: Alemtsehay Paulos, state minister for Health
a2978.name: Alemtsehay Paulos
a2978.title: state minister for Health
a2978.speech: Confirmed that a letter from the regional health bureau requesting reimbursement was sent to the Ministry of Peace, copied to the Ministry of Health.

a2978.speaker: Gizachew Muluneh, communications affairs director of the Amhara Regional Administration
a2978.name: Gizachew Muluneh
a2978.title: communications affairs director of the Amhara Regional Administration
a2978.speech: Confirmed that a budget request has already been sent to the federal government: “We've incurred high costs for measures that required immediate intervention [from the regional government],” he told Fortune.

a2978.speaker: Hospital sources at Finote Ghion Hospital (anonymous)
a2978.name: Hospital sources at Finote Ghion Hospital (anonymous)
a2978.speech: Said the Hospital sent some of its medics to the war front in the Western Command, deployed to provide treatments on the battlefront: “Psychiatrists are still serving in these areas” ; Disclosed that in addition to members of the national army, the Hospital has been providing care for members of the Amhara special forces.

a2978.speaker: Health worker who requested to remain anonymous due to the issue's sensitivity
a2978.name: Health worker who requested to remain anonymous due to the issue's sensitivity
a2978.speech: Said the radiology department of the Hospital sees up to four heavily injured patients a week, and that the number was double during the early days of the conflict.

a2978.speaker: Federal authorities (Ethiopia)
a2978.name: Federal authorities (Ethiopia)
a2978.speech: Claim that no less than 70pc of spendings to feed the millions of people displaced in Tigray Regional State is paid by the government.

a2978.speaker: Andualem Tilahun (PhD), macroeconomist
a2978.name: Andualem Tilahun (PhD)
a2978.title: macroeconomist
a2978.speech: Said fiscal risks of different natures can be addressed using various techniques: recurring and anticipated shocks like drought can be managed through contingency budgeting and midterm shocks can be addressed through reserves insurance, but unanticipated shocks like these cannot be solved through reserves or insurance; what remains as a possible solution is to cut the budget from other projects or expenditures and finance immediate deficit or borrowing, citing that slashing funding for other areas or projects will likely aggravate economic issues stemming from the COVID-19 pandemic, while borrowing could cause more inflation: “Both are unfavourable choices” ; Advised that having budget discipline that creates a fiscal space capable of accommodating such shocks would have allowed the government to better manage the situation, and that non-inflationary borrowing to bridge the budget deficit could be the best way to go.

a2978.speaker: International Organisation for Migration (IOM) (assessments conducted in April)
a2978.name: International Organisation for Migration (IOM) (assessments conducted in April)
a2978.speech: The crisis in Tigray has displaced nearly 1.6 million people since the conflict began, according to assessments conducted in April by the International Organisation for Migration (IOM).

a2978.speaker: USAID (report released on April 28)
a2978.name: USAID (report released on April 28)
a2978.speech: “Active hostilities have been reported across all of Tigray’s six zones in recent weeks, while volatile security conditions have rendered some previously accessible woredas - or districts - inaccessible.”

a3145.speaker: Donald Trump, U.S. President
a3145.name: Donald Trump
a3145.title: U.S. President
a3145.speech: “Where did you learn to speak so beautifully?” Trump asked, prompting laughter ; “That’s very interesting. It’s beautiful English.”

a3145.speaker: Joseph N. Boakai, President of Liberia
a3145.name: Joseph N. Boakai
a3145.title: President of Liberia

a3145.speaker: Joseph N. Boakai, President of Liberia
a3145.name: Joseph N. Boakai
a3145.title: President of Liberia
a3145.speech: Made a direct appeal to Trump, calling for increased American investment in Liberia, listing the country’s rich natural resource potential as an opportunity for American investors; boasted of Liberia’s stability in the region, citing successive democratic elections, and reminded Trump of Liberia’s historic ties with the United States while commending President Trump’s policies ; “Liberia is a longtime friend of the United States. We believe in your policy of making America great again, and we go a long way with you in your diplomacy that promotes economic development and commercial friendship.” ; “We are committed to peace, and we’ve been very lucky within our region. We are a country that has had a series of democratic elections, and our country has been cooling down.” ; “One of the things we ask, as good friends for a long time, is the opportunity to do a survey of our minerals... We’d like to see that happen.”

a3145.speaker: Center for Global Development (report)
a3145.name: Center for Global Development (report)
a3145.speech: According to the Center for Global Development, U.S. aid to Liberia amounted to 2.6 percent of the country’s gross national income, the highest percentage of any nation in the world.

a3449.speaker: Craig Hart, USAID Mission Director for Tanzania
a3449.name: Craig Hart
a3449.title: USAID Mission Director for Tanzania
a3449.speech: Said during the visit that USAID will continue supporting programs that make an impact that matters in Lindi Region and complement the Government of Tanzania's effort in improving access to quality health services in Lindi; when he visited Sokoine Regional Referral Hospital, talked about the USAID support over years and supported services including those supported by the USAID Afya Yangu Southern Project, and acknowledged their capacity to manage direct funding as well as showcasing the regional sustainability plan/road map and what has been achieved so far.

a3503.speaker: Valery Mikhailov, Ambassador of the Russian Federation to Burundi
a3503.name: Valery Mikhailov
a3503.title: Ambassador of the Russian Federation to Burundi
a3503.speech: Affirms that, over the past 63 years, relations between the two countries, which share part of their history, have centred on mutual respect, trust and the defence of common interests in favour of their respective peoples: "This year we are celebrating the 63rd anniversary of their establishment. Already in the Soviet era, our country provided its assistance to Burundi. And today the Russian Federation, as the legitimate heir of the USSR, continues this cooperation in various fields. We regularly provide humanitarian aid and send Burundian students to study in Russian universities. At present, more than one hundred scholarships are granted each year, and we note with satisfaction that the graduates of these programmes occupy positions of responsibility in their country. Such extensive cooperation contributes to strengthening friendship and mutual understanding between our peoples."

a3503.speaker: Valery Mikhailov, Ambassador of the Russian Federation to Burundi
a3503.name: Valery Mikhailov
a3503.title: Ambassador of the Russian Federation to Burundi
a3503.speech: "An important achievement of our cooperation is the constant mutual support we give each other on international platforms. Russia and Burundi strictly respect the principles of sovereignty, non-interference in internal affairs and rejection of unilateral sanctions and double standards, which guarantees stability and predictability in bilateral and multilateral formats. This approach not only strengthens trust between our countries, but also gives significant impetus to the development of joint projects and to the effective resolution of global and regional challenges."

a3503.speaker: Valery Mikhailov, Ambassador of the Russian Federation to Burundi
a3503.name: Valery Mikhailov
a3503.title: Ambassador of the Russian Federation to Burundi
a3503.speech: On challenges: "In the course of these six decades of mutually beneficial cooperation, our relations have not experienced any major crisis. Thanks to the convergence of our positions on the international stage and to the conviction that any dispute must be resolved solely through dialogue, we know how to listen to each other and reach concerted solutions. Any occasional misunderstanding is removed within the framework of constructive dialogue. This interaction founded on mutual respect and trust allows us to strengthen our partnership effectively."

a3503.speaker: Valery Mikhailov, Ambassador of the Russian Federation to Burundi
a3503.name: Valery Mikhailov
a3503.title: Ambassador of the Russian Federation to Burundi
a3503.speech: On the main fields of cooperation: "Our cooperation is developing in many fields such as public health, with the creation and equipping of a Russian-Burundian Centre within Burundi's National Institute of Public Health; in the energy sector, with the signing in Saint Petersburg in July 2023 of the cooperation agreement on the peaceful use of atomic energy; in the humanitarian field, with the opening of a Russian-language room of the 'Russkiy Mir' Foundation at the University of Burundi, the organization of Russian courses and cultural activities, including the screening of Russian films; in the education sector, with an annual quota of one hundred scholarships for Burundian citizens in Russian universities. There is also the specialized training of Burundian military personnel and security agents in Russian establishments, and emergency management with the development of a Crisis Management Centre project with the participation of the Russian Ministry of Emergency Situations. These lines of work reflect the shared interest in sustainable development and the well-being of our peoples."

a3503.speaker: Valery Mikhailov, Ambassador of the Russian Federation to Burundi
a3503.name: Valery Mikhailov
a3503.title: Ambassador of the Russian Federation to Burundi
a3503.speech: On future prospects: "We are convinced that bilateral relations between Russia and Burundi will continue to strengthen. This is attested by the participation of the Burundian President, Evariste Ndayishimiye, in the 2023 Russia-Africa Summit, the visit of the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation Mr. Shingiro and the signing of the Memorandum on political consultations between the foreign ministries of our two countries in November 2024, as well as the visit of the President of the Senate of Burundi, Emmanuel Sinzohagera, to Saint Petersburg during the 11th Neva International Ecological Congress in May 2025. Another high point will be the elections scheduled in Burundi on 5 June 2025, in which a Russian parliamentary delegation will take part as an observer. This is one more step towards strengthening trust, broadening dialogue and launching joint initiatives in the political, economic and humanitarian fields."

a3503.speaker: Valery Mikhailov, Ambassador of the Russian Federation to Burundi
a3503.name: Valery Mikhailov
a3503.title: Ambassador of the Russian Federation to Burundi
a3503.speech: On projects under way in Burundi: "To date, several important projects are being implemented through the Embassy. We are actively promoting the Russian language, we have delivered a large consignment of humanitarian aid, we are taking part in the creation of an Emergency Situations Management Centre and in the delivery of specialized equipment for the Russian-Burundian Centre attached to the National Institute of Public Health (INSP), and we are preparing cooperation agreements between the Burundian and Russian parliamentary chambers, etc. We see great potential for further strengthening our cooperation in many fields such as youth and educational programmes, interaction between prosecutors general, security and oversight bodies, development of the agro-industrial complex and environmental initiatives, intensification of interparliamentary dialogue, and regular exchanges of delegations and good practices. These lines of work will allow our countries to broaden their mutually beneficial partnership and bring concrete benefit to the Russian and Burundian peoples."

a3519.speaker: Somali officials
a3519.name: Somali officials
a3519.speech: Said diphtheria cases and deaths have risen sharply this year in Somalia, where the response has been curtailed by vaccine shortages and U.S. aid cuts.

a3519.speaker: Hussein Abdukar Muhidin, general director of Somalia's National Institute of Health
a3519.name: Hussein Abdukar Muhidin
a3519.title: general director of Somalia's National Institute of Health
a3519.speech: Said more than 1,600 cases, including 87 deaths, have been recorded, up from 838 cases and 56 deaths in all of 2024.

a3519.speaker: Hussein Abdukar Muhidin, general director of Somalia's National Institute of Health
a3519.name: Hussein Abdukar Muhidin
a3519.title: general director of Somalia's National Institute of Health
a3519.speech: Separately echoed the Health Minister's comments about the closure of health centres.

a3519.speaker: Deka Mohamed Ali, mother of four children who contracted diphtheria
a3519.name: Deka Mohamed Ali
a3519.title: mother of four children who contracted diphtheria
a3519.speech: “My children got sick and I just stayed at home because I did not know it was diphtheria,” she told Reuters from the bedside of her 3-year-old son Musa Abdullahi whose throat was swollen to the size of a lemon from the infection.

a3519.speaker: Ali Haji Adam, Health Minister of Somalia
a3519.name: Ali Haji Adam
a3519.title: Health Minister of Somalia
a3519.speech: Said the government had struggled to procure enough vaccines due to a global shortage and that U.S. aid cuts were making it difficult to distribute the doses it had ; “The U.S. aid cut terribly affected the health funds it used to provide to Somalia. Many health centres closed. Mobile vaccination teams that took vaccines to remote areas lost funding and now do not work.”

a3519.speaker: U.S. government statistics
a3519.name: U.S. government statistics
a3519.speech: Overall U.S. foreign assistance commitments to Somalia stand at $149 million for the fiscal year that ends on September 30, compared with $765 million in the previous fiscal year, according to U.S. government statistics.

a3519.speaker: U.S. State Department spokesperson
a3519.name: U.S. State Department spokesperson
a3519.speech: “The United States continues to provide lifesaving foreign assistance in Somalia,” said when asked about the impact of its aid cuts in the country. “America is the most generous nation in the world, and we urge other nations to dramatically increase their humanitarian efforts.”

a3519.speaker: Save the Children (aid group)
a3519.name: Save the Children (aid group)
a3519.speech: Said last month that the closure of hundreds of health clinics in Somalia this year due to foreign cuts has contributed to a doubling in the number of combined cases of diphtheria, measles, whooping cough, cholera and severe respiratory infections since mid-April.

a3519.speaker: Amnesty International
a3519.name: Amnesty International
a3519.speech: Said Somalia's government in 2024 allocated 4.8% of its budget to health, down from 8.5% the previous year, amid criticism from doctors and human rights activists of its limited funding of the health sector.

a3519.speaker: Somali health ministry (non-response)
a3519.name: Somali health ministry (non-response)
a3519.speech: The health ministry did not respond to a question about that criticism. It has said it is planning to launch a vaccination drive but has not given details when.

a3574.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a3574.name: Donald Trump
a3574.title: US President
a3574.speech: Said South Africa was pursuing what he called “unjust and immoral practices” against the white minority Afrikaner community and by filing a genocide case against Israel in the International Court of Justice in December 2023. ; Threatened to cut future funding over what he termed “terrible things, horrible things” the country's leadership was doing, and accused South Africa, without any basis in fact, of “confiscating land” and “doing things that are perhaps far worse than that”. ; In his executive order, also accused South Africa of a “shocking disregard of its citizens' rights” and taking “aggressive positions” against the US and its ally Israel in its ICJ case.

a3574.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a3574.name: Donald Trump
a3574.title: US President
a3574.speech: In 2018, during his first presidency, he accused South African authorities of the “large-scale killing of farmers” and asked his then secretary of state to look into the matter of the government “seizing land from white farmers”.

a3574.speaker: US embassy in South Africa
a3574.name: US embassy in South Africa
a3574.speech: Has subsequently said that funding from Pepfar, an American programme countering the global spread of HIV, will not be affected, adding the caveat that “not all Pepfar activities will resume”.

a3574.speaker: Conservative Afrikaner lobby groups, including AfriForum and Solidarity
a3574.name: Conservative Afrikaner lobby groups
a3574.title: including AfriForum and Solidarity
a3574.speech: Want the government to repeal what it calls “race-based laws” such as affirmative action and black economic empowerment.

a3574.speaker: Elon Musk, tech billionaire and close adviser to Trump
a3574.name: Elon Musk
a3574.title: tech billionaire and close adviser to Trump
a3574.speech: Questioned on X why Ramaphosa had “openly racist ownership laws”.

a3574.speaker: Dr Oscar van Heerden, political analyst at the University of Johannesburg
a3574.name: Dr Oscar van Heerden
a3574.title: political analyst at the University of Johannesburg
a3574.speech: Told the BBC there had “never been this kind of radical action taken to the point of an executive order being signed”. ; Put the change in dynamics partly down to “global shifts” and “new competition driving up against the US” from the likes of China, India and Brazil.

a3574.speaker: Dr Oscar van Heerden, political analyst at the University of Johannesburg
a3574.name: Dr Oscar van Heerden
a3574.title: political analyst at the University of Johannesburg
a3574.speech: Added that even if the Agoa agreement was not renewed, or South Africa ended up being excluded, those businesses currently benefiting from it would suffer short-term losses but would manage to bounce back in a few years. ; Said at the moment President Ramaphosa's government was opting for the diplomatic route – though the Trump administration's seeming lack of interest in diplomacy drastically reduced chances of success. ; Suggests the government could opt to “negotiate hard” and use the minerals it supplies to the US as a “bargaining chip”, but warns: “South Africa is going to have to think very carefully about how they play this chess game [where] the opening gambit has already been made by President Trump and Elon Musk.”

a3574.speaker: Donald MacKay, CEO of Johannesburg-based trade consulting firm XA Global Trade Advisors
a3574.name: Donald MacKay
a3574.title: CEO of Johannesburg-based trade consulting firm XA Global Trade Advisors
a3574.speech: Said that while the US was one of South Africa's biggest partners, it was not its “closest trading partner”. ; “Over the years, that relationship has waxed and waned. It's never been terribly strong [since white-minority rule ended in South Africa]. But at the same time, I think it also never deteriorated quite as much as it has in recent years and I don't think it's South Africa's fault” ; But he admitted South Africa had done “a lot” in recent years to irritate the US: “Those irritations get to accumulate and under President Trump… this is seen as an opportunity to put South Africa in its place.”

a3574.speaker: Donald MacKay, CEO of XA Global Trade Advisors
a3574.name: Donald MacKay
a3574.title: CEO of XA Global Trade Advisors
a3574.speech: Said he would be surprised if South Africa continued benefiting from the Agoa preferential agreement after the review: “My instinct is, whatever the reason that Trump is upset with South Africa, at the moment Agoa would be the easiest mechanism to use to punish South Africa.” ; Believes it will be difficult for South Africa and other nations to navigate relations with the US under “the most unpredictable politician in the world”, suggesting that they will have to increasingly see Brics as an alternative partner.

a3574.speaker: Experts (collectively, cited in the article)
a3574.name: Experts (collectively
a3574.title: cited in the article)
a3574.speech: While experts spoke on the benefits of Agoa, which is coming up for review later this year, they agreed that the impact might not be as significant as some fear; experts also fear Trump may go on to use this opportunity to end preferential access to the US market through Agoa.

a3574.speaker: South African government
a3574.name: South African government
a3574.speech: Issued a vehement rebuttal of Trump's accusations, in the face of which he doubled down.

a3574.speaker: Ronald Lamola, South Africa's Foreign Minister
a3574.name: Ronald Lamola
a3574.title: South Africa's Foreign Minister
a3574.speech: Gave a blunt response on Wednesday to Trump's move, saying there was “no chance” that South Africa would withdraw its case against Israel at the ICJ: “Standing by our principles sometimes has consequences, but we remain firm that this is important for the world, and the rule of law,” Lamola told the Financial Times.

a3574.speaker: Government of Israel
a3574.name: Government of Israel
a3574.speech: Denies South Africa's allegation that Israel has committed genocide against Palestinians living in Gaza.

a3574.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa (in his capacity as G20 president)
a3574.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a3574.title: President of South Africa (in his capacity as G20 president)
a3574.speech: Has announced he will be sending a delegation around the world to clarify South Africa's domestic and foreign policies – with Washington being a key stop.

a3574.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a3574.name: Marco Rubio
a3574.title: US Secretary of State
a3574.speech: Has announced that he will not attend a G20 meeting of foreign ministers taking place next week in Johannesburg: “My job is to advance America's national interests, not waste taxpayer money or coddle anti-Americanism.”

a3574.speaker: António Costa, president of the European Council
a3574.name: António Costa
a3574.title: president of the European Council
a3574.speech: Posted on X on Monday that he had spoken to Ramaphosa by phone to highlight the “EU's commitment to deepen ties with South Africa”.

a3731.speaker: US Mission (announcement)
a3731.name: US Mission (announcement)
