a3731.speech: Announced the arrival of new Consul General, Rick Swart, in Lagos.

a3731.speaker: Rick Swart, US Consul General in Lagos
a3731.name: Rick Swart
a3731.title: US Consul General in Lagos
a3731.speech: “I am honored to serve in Nigeria. I am excited about the opportunity to travel across the region, meet the people, experience the culture, and advance the shared goals of making our two countries safer, stronger, and more prosperous.” ; “I thank JoEllen for her remarkable leadership and for the outstanding work she has done to promote our close partnership with the Nigerian people in the region.” ; “I look forward to working closely with Ambassador Mills and the team at the U.S. Embassy in Abuja to further advance the shared objectives between Nigeria and the United States.”

a3888.speaker: Rami Khouri, American University of Beirut
a3888.name: Rami Khouri
a3888.title: American University of Beirut
a3888.speech: Stressed that Arab governments and their external sponsors tend to prioritize the wrong threats. Most Arab governments continue to introduce superficial reforms in pivotal sectors such as education, employment, and anti-corruption, but their efforts mostly remain unsuccessful or limited in their impact... The Arab region and many individual countries are literally being ripped apart by the consequences of decades of incompetent, autocratic governance, combined with continuing foreign military interventions and the impacts of the century-old Arab-Israeli conflict.

a3888.speaker: Rami Khouri, American University of Beirut
a3888.name: Rami Khouri
a3888.title: American University of Beirut
a3888.speech: According to Rami Khouri, the symptoms of the systemic crisis started to appear several decades ago. They could have been alleviated much more easily at the outset had governments been more effective in recognizing and tackling the issues that plagued their citizens, especially corruption, insufficient decent jobs, state cronyism, and declining educational standards. Rather than dealing with these early signs of serious mass internal dysfunction, regimes focused on military security and internal repression. The outcome was to exacerbate rather than solve the threats to social cohesion and national well-being, which in turn contributed to the brisk emigration of educated youth, the collapse of political parties, the rise of sectarian groups and militias, and steady expansion in adherents to both nonviolent and militant Islamist movements.

a3888.speaker: Khalid Abu-Ismail, 2018 study "Poverty and Vulnerability in Arab States"
a3888.name: Khalid Abu-Ismail
a3888.title: 2018 study "Poverty and Vulnerability in Arab States"
a3888.speech: Stated that the actual levels of poverty and vulnerability in the Arab region are higher than previously thought, with some two-thirds of citizens falling into the categories of poor or vulnerable. The realities of declining family wellbeing were disguised by prevailing poverty measures based on daily expenditures, which did not accurately capture two critical trends: high levels of poverty, and rising levels of vulnerability among families that used to be counted among the middle class or middle-income category, but have gradually fallen into the poor or vulnerable categories.

a3888.speaker: Economists at UNDP, the UN Economic and Social Commission for Western Asia (ESCWA), the World Bank and other institutions (research)
a3888.name: Economists at UNDP
a3888.title: the UN Economic and Social Commission for Western Asia (ESCWA), the World Bank and other institutions (research)
a3888.speech: Significant research in recent years has used the Multi-Dimensional Poverty (MDP) measure to gauge poverty and vulnerability more accurately than the previous reliance on money-metric measures such as $1.25 or $1.90 expenditures per day. The Multi-Dimensional Poverty figures indicate poverty rates as much as four times higher than previously assumed.

a3888.speaker: ESCWA economists
a3888.name: ESCWA economists
a3888.speech: According to ESCWA economists who have analyzed this issue, the middle class in non-oil-producing states has shrunk from 45 percent to 33 percent of the population. They see many middle income families sliding into vulnerability, and vulnerable families in turn falling into poverty.

a3888.speaker: Khalid Abu-Ismail
a3888.name: Khalid Abu-Ismail
a3888.speech: Noted that the drivers of this increase in poverty and vulnerability have persisted or worsened since the 2010-11 Arab uprisings. They are likely to drive further families into poverty and vulnerability for years to come, given the current regional realities.

a3888.speaker: Khalid Abu-Ismail
a3888.name: Khalid Abu-Ismail
a3888.speech: Further argued that this trend seems to be directly associated with the steady recent decline in the quality of state-managed basic social services, mainly outside the Gulf region, including health care, education, water, electricity, transport, and social safety nets.

a3888.speaker: ESCWA (calculations)
a3888.name: ESCWA (calculations)
a3888.speech: The number of Arabs requiring humanitarian assistance to stay alive and minimally healthy, according to ESCWA calculations, is 60 million people in seven crisis states. They include many of the 30 million people who have been displaced in the Arab region in recent years.

a3888.speaker: 2019 MENA Economic Monitor report
a3888.name: 2019 MENA Economic Monitor report
a3888.speech: Indicated that once families fall into poverty, they are likely to remain there for generations to come.

a3888.speaker: IMF and other projections
a3888.name: IMF and other projections
a3888.speech: Say the Arab region must create 60-100 million jobs by 2030, and 27 million jobs in the next five years, to reduce unemployment significantly.

a3932.speaker: Lotus Resources (Australian firm)
a3932.name: Lotus Resources (Australian firm)
a3932.speech: “Kayelekera is a world-class asset,” Lotus told investors at this week’s Macquarie Australia Conference. “It’s key to the global energy transition.”

a3932.speaker: Lotus Resources (the company)
a3932.name: Lotus Resources (the company)
a3932.speech: The company says local hiring remains a priority (over 90% of the mine's original workforce was Malawian).

a3932.speaker: Malawi's Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority
a3932.name: Malawi's Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority
a3932.speech: In May 2025 conditionally approved the restart, with the condition that strict environmental monitoring and community consultation must continue.

a3932.speaker: Activists from the Natural Resources Justice Network
a3932.name: Activists from the Natural Resources Justice Network
a3932.speech: Warn of radiation risks, waste management concerns, and lack of community benefit-sharing; they demand full transparency before operations ramp up.

a4016.speaker: H.E. Chen Zhihong, Chinese Ambassador to Mali
a4016.name: H.E. Chen Zhihong
a4016.title: Chinese Ambassador to Mali
a4016.speech: Wrote that the United States has recently imposed tariffs, under various pretexts, on all of its trading partners, including China and African countries, seriously compromising the legitimate rights and interests of nations, seriously violating WTO rules, seriously harming the rules-based multilateral trading system and seriously disrupting the stability of the world economic order ; “The world must embrace equity and multilateralism, and oppose hegemony.”

a4016.speaker: Chinese government
a4016.name: Chinese government
a4016.speech: Strongly condemns this measure and firmly opposes it.

a4016.speaker: H.E. Chen Zhihong, Chinese Ambassador to Mali
a4016.name: H.E. Chen Zhihong
a4016.title: Chinese Ambassador to Mali
a4016.speech: Argued that the American measures violate fundamental economic principles and market norms and that using tariffs as a weapon of extreme pressure for selfish ends is a typical example of unilateralism, protectionism and economic bullying; under the cover of so-called “reciprocity,” the United States engages in zero-sum games and essentially pursues “America First” and “American exceptionalism,” exploiting tariffs to overturn the existing international economic and trade order and sacrificing the legitimate interests of countries worldwide to serve its own hegemonic agenda.

a4016.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Minister of Foreign Affairs
a4016.name: Wang Yi
a4016.title: Chinese Minister of Foreign Affairs
a4016.speech: Posed the following questions: Has the trade deficit increased or decreased? Has manufacturing become more competitive or less competitive? Has inflation eased or worsened? Are Americans living better or worse?

a4016.speaker: H.E. Chen Zhihong, Chinese Ambassador to Mali
a4016.name: H.E. Chen Zhihong
a4016.title: Chinese Ambassador to Mali
a4016.speech: Warned that the American tariff increases will disrupt global supply chains, raise production costs at every stage of the industrial chain, drive up logistics costs, distort the allocation of market resources, cause turbulence in financial markets and heighten the risks of economic recession.

a4016.speaker: World Trade Organization (rules)
a4016.name: World Trade Organization (rules)
a4016.speech: Clearly stipulates that its members must not unilaterally raise customs tariffs, but must resolve disputes through negotiation.

a4016.speaker: H.E. Chen Zhihong, Chinese Ambassador to Mali
a4016.name: H.E. Chen Zhihong
a4016.title: Chinese Ambassador to Mali
a4016.speech: Said Africa is also a victim of American unilateralism and protectionism: at a time when African countries are striving to promote their national development, the imposition of US tariffs disrupts the pace of the global recovery and inflicts unwarranted shocks on the African economy; the renewal of the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) is becoming uncertain, not to mention the brutal shutdown of USAID and the suspension of its ongoing projects, all of which exacerbates the continent’s economic vulnerability.

a4016.speaker: H.E. Chen Zhihong, Chinese Ambassador to Mali
a4016.name: H.E. Chen Zhihong
a4016.title: Chinese Ambassador to Mali
a4016.speech: Said that unlike the United States, China will continue to open its doors ever wider; recalled that at the 2024 FOCAC Summit China announced zero-tariff treatment for 100% of tariff lines for the least developed African countries maintaining diplomatic relations with it, and stated that China is ready to cooperate with all friendly countries to adhere to genuine multilateralism, jointly oppose all forms of unilateralism and protectionism, and defend the international system with the United Nations at its centre and the multilateral trading system centred on the WTO.

a4080.speaker: Kinday Samba, WFP Director in Niger
a4080.name: Kinday Samba
a4080.title: WFP Director in Niger
a4080.speech: Thanked Russia for its contribution to the activities of the World Organization in the country and stressed that thanks to this Russian assistance, it was possible to cover the consumption of sunflower oil for a period of three months for the most vulnerable populations, including refugees.

a4080.speaker: Russian Federation (statement)
a4080.name: Russian Federation (statement)
a4080.speech: "Russia, for its part, will continue to provide the necessary humanitarian support to the people of the Republic of Niger, a friendly country."

a4287.speaker: Tafele Kapatuka, woman from Mwenda Village, TA Chadza, Lilongwe
a4287.name: Tafele Kapatuka
a4287.title: woman from Mwenda Village, TA Chadza, Lilongwe
a4287.speech: “I was afraid of getting pregnant again. I already have five children and four of them were unplanned. The thought of another unplanned pregnancy was killing me” ; “He could not understand. He started accusing me of sleeping with other men. I could not afford to travel to the health facility either. It is far and we do not have money for transport.”

a4287.speaker: Ruth Mailosi, woman from Mwenda Village
a4287.name: Ruth Mailosi
a4287.title: woman from Mwenda Village
a4287.speech: “I spoke to our Community-Based Distribution Agent (CBDA), who told me that the outreach clinic would no longer be coming because American donors had withdrawn their support.”

a4287.speaker: Community-Based Distribution Agent (CBDA), Mwenda Village
a4287.name: Community-Based Distribution Agent (CBDA)
a4287.title: Mwenda Village
a4287.speech: Told Ruth Mailosi that the outreach clinic would no longer be coming because American donors had withdrawn their support.

a4287.speaker: Patuma Machira, community volunteer in Mwenda Village
a4287.name: Patuma Machira
a4287.title: community volunteer in Mwenda Village
a4287.speech: “People here are now completely cut off from basic health services. The nearest facility is far and most people either walk or use bicycles, which is not practical, especially for women and children.”

a4287.speaker: Elina Kachingwe, mother from the area
a4287.name: Elina Kachingwe
a4287.title: mother from the area
a4287.speech: “I had all my antenatal visits at the outreach clinic. It was convenient and saved us a lot of money. When the clinic stopped and my delivery time came, I had to walk a long distance to Bwaila Hospital and I gave birth on the way.”

a4287.speaker: Doreen Ali, Head of the Reproductive Health Directorate, Ministry of Health (Malawi)
a4287.name: Doreen Ali
a4287.title: Head of the Reproductive Health Directorate, Ministry of Health (Malawi)
a4287.speech: Says that despite shifts in funding from some partners, Malawi remains committed to accelerating the implementation of health programmes for women, newborns and adolescents ; indicates that the ministry has conducted an evaluation to analyse how the funding cut will affect operations and goals.

a4287.speaker: Doreen Ali, Head of the Reproductive Health Directorate, Ministry of Health (Malawi)
a4287.name: Doreen Ali
a4287.title: Head of the Reproductive Health Directorate, Ministry of Health (Malawi)
a4287.speech: “With reduced resources, we are in the process of identifying non-essential expenditures that can be cut or postponed so that we maintain only our core functions” ; while admitting that the funding cut is a major blow to the gains made, says the Ministry is in the process of engaging with the Ministry of Finance to increase domestic financing to bridge the gap and to lobby support from the private sector ; “We have integrated most services and are exploring alternative funding sources. We shall continue prioritising service delivery and integration because right now our aim is to do more with less funding and minimise losses from the gains we have made as a nation.”

a4287.speaker: Reproductive Health Directorate, Ministry of Health (Malawi)
a4287.name: Reproductive Health Directorate
a4287.title: Ministry of Health (Malawi)
a4287.speech: According to the Directorate, Malawi has made progress across all areas of sexual and reproductive health and rights, including maternal, newborn and child health, over the past decades, driven by investments that have strengthened primary healthcare delivery and improved access to quality services at the community level.

a4287.speaker: World Health Organisation
a4287.name: World Health Organisation
a4287.speech: According to the WHO, Malawi’s maternal mortality rate stands at 225 per 100,000 live births, against a target of 70 per 100,000 by 2030.

a4287.speaker: Maziko Matemba, health rights activist
a4287.name: Maziko Matemba
a4287.title: health rights activist
a4287.speech: Says it is concerning that many USAid-funded family planning projects have been severely impacted by the aid freeze; that in some targeted communities already grappling with poor indicators in family planning, STI prevention and HIV infections, the progress made is beginning to erode, signalling a worrying reversal ; “This setback is largely due to the abrupt closure of critical health interventions, many of which lacked sustainability plans at the time of their termination. If Malawi fails to secure sustained support, whether through domestic resources or international aid, within the next six to twelve months, the situation could become critical.”

a4309.speaker: Statement released Thursday (on the AXIAN Telecom / EIB Global project)
a4309.name: Statement released Thursday (on the AXIAN Telecom / EIB Global project)
a4309.speech: According to the statement, Tanzania is expected to double its 4G coverage following the new US$100 million project by AXIAN Telecom aimed at supporting the expansion of its mobile broadband network infrastructure across Tanzania and Madagascar; US$60 million of the financing will benefit Tanzania and US$40 million will go to Madagascar.

a4309.speaker: Hassan Jaber, CEO of AXIAN Telecom
a4309.name: Hassan Jaber
a4309.title: CEO of AXIAN Telecom
a4309.speech: Said the US$100 million EIB Global financing will help the company expand mobile phone infrastructure in Madagascar and Tanzania and benefit millions of people, adding: “This new large-scale network investment will pave the way for socio-economic growth, digital inclusion, and better opportunities.”

a4309.speaker: Ambroise Fayolle, European Investment Bank Vice-President
a4309.name: Ambroise Fayolle
a4309.title: European Investment Bank Vice-President
a4309.speech: Said that digital connectivity opens doors for education, business, healthcare and social inclusion, which he believes is critical to any country’s development ; “This new investment demonstrates the EIB’s commitment to empowering communities, fostering sustainable development, and driving positive change through enhanced access to affordable high-speed communications.”

a4309.speaker: European Union Ambassadors to Madagascar and Tanzania
a4309.name: European Union Ambassadors to Madagascar and Tanzania
a4309.speech: Have expressed their support for the EIB’s investment and its significant impact on the countries’ development.

a4309.speaker: Christine Grau, EU Ambassador to Tanzania
a4309.name: Christine Grau
a4309.title: EU Ambassador to Tanzania
a4309.speech: Said that the organisation is a key partner for Tanzania in advancing the government’s digital transformation agenda, from policy support to infrastructure and investments ; “This EIB Global investment in AXIAN Telecom, made possible through a European Union guarantee, is a concrete example of our commitment to invest in digital connectivity” ; “The European Union believes that in the area of connectivity, reinforcing public-private partnerships is crucial for a human-centric model of digital transformation to ensure that no one is left behind.”

a4336.speaker: Ejiro Okotie, Gender and Social Inclusion Specialist and Focal Person for the Open Government Partnership Coordinating for USAID State2State
a4336.name: Ejiro Okotie
a4336.title: Gender and Social Inclusion Specialist and Focal Person for the Open Government Partnership Coordinating for USAID State2State
a4336.speech: Said the gathering was a quarterly progress and review meeting to see how the OGP is being implemented in Ebonyi state, the challenges being faced and to discuss strategies to enhance OGP SAP implementation ; "Also to chat a way for sustainability of the partnership between state actors and non state actors as State2State will soon be rounding off their programme in the state come August 2025 and there is need for early plans for consolidating reforms achievement supported so far."

a4336.speaker: Dr Moses Onwe, Director of Statistics in the Ebonyi State Ministry of Budget and Planning
a4336.name: Dr Moses Onwe
a4336.title: Director of Statistics in the Ebonyi State Ministry of Budget and Planning
a4336.speech: Said that the working ethics of OGP have been beneficial to the citizens as the general public knows more about the activities of the state government.

a4336.speaker: Mrs Nwafor Lorrieth, Programme Manager of Initiative for Social Change in Africa
a4336.name: Mrs Nwafor Lorrieth
a4336.title: Programme Manager of Initiative for Social Change in Africa
a4336.speech: Harped on the freedom of Information dissemination of the activities of Open Government Partnership in the State.

a4336.speaker: Thematic working groups at the meeting (group presentations)
a4336.name: Thematic working groups at the meeting (group presentations)
a4336.speech: Made presentations with the recommendation that OGP projects should be included in the 2025 budget call circular to aid budgetary provisions for OGP implementation in the 2025 Budget.

a4344.speaker: Eswatini Communications Commission (ESCCOM) annual report for the financial year ended 31 March
a4344.name: Eswatini Communications Commission (ESCCOM) annual report for the financial year ended 31 March
a4344.speech: Found that Samsung cellphone users in Eswatini cannot access Eswatini Mobile's 5G network, following the commission's 5G network tests: "The commission conducted its own drive test and speed test exercise. This is in line with the commission's mandate to ensure that all communications services are provided in a manner that will best promote economic and social development." ; recorded the average download speed achieved by Eswatini Mobile's 5G network at 293 Mbps ; "Moreover, the exercise also revealed that Samsung phones cannot access Eswatini Mobile's 5G network at the moment, yet about 46% of devices on the mobile operator's network are Samsung devices."

a4344.speaker: Eswatini Communications Commission (ESCCOM) annual report for the financial year ended 31 March
a4344.name: Eswatini Communications Commission (ESCCOM) annual report for the financial year ended 31 March
a4344.speech: "Eswatini Mobile failed to meet the accessibility KPIs for 2G and 3G, 4G user throughput download speed, and the target of more than 99% on 4G cell availability." ; reported that MTN Eswatini complied with its license obligations for 2G and 3G, but failed to meet the set target of 20 Mbps on 4G user throughput download speed and the target of more than 99% on 4G cell availability.

a4344.speaker: Eswatini Communications Commission (ESCCOM) annual report for the financial year ended 31 March
a4344.name: Eswatini Communications Commission (ESCCOM) annual report for the financial year ended 31 March
a4344.speech: Reported that about 62% of imported communication devices were found not to meet ESCCOM standards during on-site inspections of 18 licensed dealers: "A total of 69 electronic communications equipment devices were inspected and only 26 devices were approved by ESCCOM. This implies that only 38% of the tested equipment was type approved while the remaining 62% was unauthorised." ; stated that this highlighted that a significant amount of equipment being imported and used in Eswatini has not been type approved, posing a challenge mainly to consumers who purchase devices that do not meet the set standards ; reported that to minimise the importation of non-type approved equipment and to operationalise a memorandum of understanding with the Eswatini Revenue Service (ERS), the commission capacitated ERS officials on the regulation of equipment imports, including how to conduct verifications through physical verifications or use of the ASYCUDA customs management system.

a4402.speaker: Dr. Melkiory Ngido, Country Manager of Barrick-Twiga
a4402.name: Dr. Melkiory Ngido
a4402.title: Country Manager of Barrick-Twiga
a4402.speech: Said that, besides paying substantial dividends, the firm has also contributed to government revenue through various levies in mining activity, and boosted the national economy.

a4402.speaker: Nehemiah Mchechu, Treasury Registrar
a4402.name: Nehemiah Mchechu
a4402.title: Treasury Registrar
a4402.speech: Said Twiga Minerals had continued recording impressive performance in the mining sector ; said this year they had collected Sh91.28 trillion in dividends, contributions, and revenue, which would be directed towards improving education, healthcare, infrastructure, and other key sectors in the country ; explained that success in collecting dividends and contributions was due to the good work done by the management and boards of various public enterprises: "Your Excellency, the boards and management of these institutions are truly implementing your vision and directives concerning the contributions of these enterprises by changing working culture and mindset, thereby improving productivity in their respective areas" ; emphasised that the vision and directives of President Dr Samia Suluhu Hassan to reform public institutions aimed at increasing production efficiency and continued generating revenue and dividends for the government: "It is crucial to ensure the seed of development that has been planted continues blossoming and bearing fruit for the greater good of our nation."

a4402.speaker: Dr Samia Suluhu Hassan, President of Tanzania
a4402.name: Dr Samia Suluhu Hassan
a4402.title: President of Tanzania
a4402.speech: Urged the Treasury Registrar to make an effort so that public institutions and enterprises continue contributing through dividends and payments to the government's central fund: "This 1.028 trillion collection is a positive step towards reducing dependency on foreign aid and beginning self-reliance" ; called on leaders of public institutions and enterprises to continue safeguarding capital and investments and minimise revenue losses to grow their incomes and increase dividend contributions to the government.

a4442.speaker: Samir Bhattacharya, interviewee (India-Africa analyst)
a4442.name: Samir Bhattacharya
a4442.title: interviewee (India-Africa analyst)
a4442.speech: "The world is going through a turbulent time... the war in Ukraine started derailing all the recovery plans... Rising food and energy prices, disruptions in the trade of commodities and services, and a sharp humanitarian crisis were brought on by a sharp decline in development funding for Africa." ; Said the continent suffers the most from the detrimental effects of climate change and that this crisis also severely impacts the already too-slow energy transition program ; "Given this background, India's contribution to Africa's reconstruction effort would be crucial... The key tenets of India's development partnership with Africa have included capacity-building initiatives, lines of credit, grant financing, small-scale development projects, technical advice, disaster relief and humanitarian support, and military cooperation. There is a strong need for India and Africa to work together in this changing global situation."

a4442.speaker: Samir Bhattacharya, interviewee (India-Africa analyst)
a4442.name: Samir Bhattacharya
a4442.title: interviewee (India-Africa analyst)
a4442.speech: On areas of collaboration to strengthen: "To achieve inclusive growth, Africa requires financial resources... In the absence of adequate local financing sources, the policymakers of the continent are grappling to arrange the finance from different traditional external partners." ; Said LOCs provided by the Export-Import Bank of India are the primary source for India to finance development projects in Africa, with over 44 African countries granted 200 Letters of Credit totalling about $12 billion up to May 2021, $2.2 billion in approved pipelines and $9.75 billion in active Lines of Credit, and a recent US$100 million credit line to the Africa Finance Corporation ; Said India has financed several significant infrastructure projects in Africa, including a railway line in Ghana, mining equipment to Zimbabwe, a city decongestion project in Zambia, LPG facilities in Mozambique and vehicles to Cote d'Ivoire, Senegal, Tanzania and Zimbabwe ; "Concerning security, India has always been at the forefront in preparing African countries' military forces for the twenty-first century's security problems. These training programs must include counterinsurgency operations, peacekeeping, marine security, and specialised instruction in emerging fields like drone operations and cyber warfare." ; Said the continent is lagging in human resource development and that "India's primary method of interaction with Africa has always been capacity building and skill development. India needs to step up its information diplomacy with Africa."

a4442.speaker: Samir Bhattacharya, interviewee (India-Africa analyst)
a4442.name: Samir Bhattacharya
a4442.title: interviewee (India-Africa analyst)
a4442.speech: On new and emerging areas of cooperation: Said African nations are realising that the blue economy presents an opportunity for Africa to develop new revenue streams that could aid in development and lessen reliance on foreign aid, and that "India and African nations working together to establish the 'Blue Economy' will have both economic and maritime security benefits." ; Said media connections between Africa and India are essentially nonexistent and that "India could attempt to create a dedicated TV channel that broadcasts content to Africa." ; Said collaboration between India and Africa on traditional medicine offers an outstanding prospect ; Said Africa loses billions of dollars every year due to illicit trading of natural resources and that "India can help Africa curb this illegal practice by sharing its experiences to improve data quality and infrastructure, skills and resources, as well as provide training to the national statistics office."

a4442.speaker: Samir Bhattacharya, interviewee (India-Africa analyst)
a4442.name: Samir Bhattacharya
a4442.title: interviewee (India-Africa analyst)
a4442.speech: On what has been achieved since the last India-Africa summit: Said the aim, methodology, and development cooperation strategies with Africa have drastically changed since the last India-Africa summit in 2015, listing increased attention to Africa's development agenda, modified LoC mechanics, new financing mechanisms, active private-sector participation, new capacity-building approaches, greater civil-society participation, digital capacity building, priority to partnering with multilateral organisations, and trilateral cooperation ; Said many ongoing development activities were affected by the COVID-19 epidemic but that digital initiatives in healthcare and education accelerated, citing India's Pan African e-Network Project, re-launched in October 2019 as e-Aarogya Bharati, and COVID-19 management training webinars for African healthcare practitioners.

a4442.speaker: Samir Bhattacharya, interviewee (India-Africa analyst)
a4442.name: Samir Bhattacharya
a4442.title: interviewee (India-Africa analyst)
a4442.speech: On increasing trade and economic relations: Said Indian trade with Africa is valued at USD 98 billion in 2022-2023 compared to USD 89.6 billion the year before, and that Africa is a sizable unexplored market for Indian manufacturers of textiles, pharmaceuticals, cars and light machinery ; Said that under the AfCFTA local supply chains and regional production networks will emerge as significant markets for Indian investments and exports, and that India should actively investigate how it might benefit from the agreement by developing a legal system forging a unique connection between the AfCFTA and India.

a4442.speaker: Samir Bhattacharya, interviewee (India-Africa analyst)
a4442.name: Samir Bhattacharya
a4442.title: interviewee (India-Africa analyst)
a4442.speech: On the next five years and a multipolar world: "Regarding geopolitics, the world is at a turning point where multipolarity is quickly replacing US unipolarity. Both India and Africa are devoted to their cooperation to establish a multipolar world order... India sees Africa's rise as essential to balance the world's power structure." ; Said India will collaborate with African nations bilaterally and in multilateral platforms like the BRICS and the G20 to promote inclusive and decentralised economic practices, and that India's development partnership with Africa is anticipated to place a strong emphasis on digital, green, healthcare, food security, and water during the next five to ten years.

a4442.speaker: African Union's 2050 Africa's Maritime Strategy and the Africa Blue Economy Strategy (2019)
a4442.name: African Union's 2050 Africa's Maritime Strategy and the Africa Blue Economy Strategy (2019)
a4442.speech: Cited as the frameworks according to which African nations are realising that the blue economy presents an opportunity for Africa to develop new revenue streams that could aid in development and lessen reliance on foreign aid.

a4442.speaker: Reuters research
a4442.name: Reuters research
a4442.speech: A Reuters research found that every year, gold worth billions of dollars is smuggled out of Africa via the United Arab Emirates in the Middle East, which serves as a gateway to markets in Europe, the United States, and other countries.

a4442.speaker: Ministry of Ayush (India)
a4442.name: Ministry of Ayush (India)
a4442.speech: According to the Ministry of Ayush, by 2025 the market for complementary and alternative medicine is anticipated to grow to $70 billion.

a4461.speaker: Anita Kiki, Deputy Special Representative of the United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS)
a4461.name: Anita Kiki
a4461.title: Deputy Special Representative of the United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS)
a4461.speech: Says the UN remains committed to supporting South Sudan’s journey toward lasting peace and stability; speaking during the United Nations Day commemoration in Juba, said this year’s event is marked under the global theme “Building Our Future Together”, and noted that the UN is celebrating 80 years since its founding, following the devastation of the Second World War.

a4461.speaker: Anita Kiki, Deputy Special Representative of the United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS)
a4461.name: Anita Kiki
a4461.title: Deputy Special Representative of the United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS)
a4461.speech: Highlighted the progress South Sudan has made through the partnership between the United Nations, the government, and the people: said adult literacy has improved from 27 percent in 2008 to just over 34 percent in 2022, while maternal deaths have fallen from about 2,000 in 2006 to around 1,200 per 100,000 live births in 2023; added that several roads and bridges have been constructed, new institutions established, and women’s representation in parliament has risen to 32 percent, up from 26 percent in 2013.

a4461.speaker: Anita Kiki, Deputy Special Representative of the United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS)
a4461.name: Anita Kiki
a4461.title: Deputy Special Representative of the United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS)
a4461.speech: Noted that insecurity and conflict continue to hinder the country’s progress; said renewed clashes and economic shocks have worsened displacement, with more than 320,000 people newly displaced this year alone, that an estimated 9.3 million people across South Sudan are in need of humanitarian assistance, and that more than 1.2 million people have crossed into the country since the outbreak of the Sudan conflict.

a4461.speaker: Anita Kiki, Deputy Special Representative of the United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS)
a4461.name: Anita Kiki
a4461.title: Deputy Special Representative of the United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS)
a4461.speech: Reaffirmed the UN’s long-standing partnership with South Sudan, recalling its support since Operation Lifeline Sudan, the Comprehensive Peace Agreement, the 2011 referendum, and the Revitalized Peace Agreement of 2018.

a4485.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of Mozambique
a4485.name: Daniel Chapo
a4485.title: President of Mozambique
a4485.speech: Said on Sunday he wanted to renegotiate the contracts for the megaprojects that exploit the country's resources: "Mozambique is no longer the same as it was 20 years ago. We're not the same people, we don't think the same way, we don't have the same goals, we don't have the same interests. Times have changed, wills have changed and challenges have also changed." ; "Because of this change, anywhere in the world, including Mozambique, when a contract needs to be renewed you have to discuss the clauses for renewing the contract. And that's what we're doing at the moment, discussing the clauses of the contract renewal between the parties so that we do not renew the exact same contract." ; "It seems like a delay, but it's not a delay as such. There are contracts in Mozambique that were signed 20 years ago. I'll give just three examples. I could give several. I'll give the example of Mozal [aluminium smelter]. And I'll give the example of Sasol [gas] in Inhambane [province], I'll give the example of Kenmare, here in Nampula province. And these contracts, after 20 years, we now need to renew."

a4485.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of Mozambique
a4485.name: Daniel Chapo
a4485.title: President of Mozambique
a4485.speech: On the negotiations with Kenmare: recalled that there are "interests to defend on both sides" when defining the contractual clauses, highlighting the concerns of the population with "corporate social responsibility" or the incorporation of local content ; "Kenmare is trying to defend its interests and we, as Mozambique's government, are trying to defend the interests of the Mozambican people. And in this defence of the interests of the Mozambican people, we're taking our time, which seems like a long time, but it's not a long time. It's really the fact that Kenmare is defending its interests, because it's an investor, it has to get a return on its investment." ; "That's why we're currently negotiating peacefully with Kenmare, and at any time, the contract will go back to the Council of Ministers. And if both parties feel that their interests are satisfied, the contract will be renewed. But because there is no conflict or problem, Kenmare has never stopped operating. It has continued to operate because the contract is being negotiated peacefully by the two parties. They don't stop operating because we think it's a completely peaceful negotiation."

a4485.speaker: Basilio Muhate (@basiliomuhate), post on X
a4485.name: Basilio Muhate (@basiliomuhate)
a4485.title: post on X
a4485.speech: "ALGUNS CONTRATOS DOS MEGA PROJECTOS DE MOCAMBIQUE SERAO REVISTOS PARA BENEFICIAR O POVO" [Some contracts of Mozambique's megaprojects will be revised to benefit the people], quoting Daniel Chapo: "Quero deixar claro, Mocambique ja nao e o mesmo de 20 anos atras, nem somos a mesmas quantidade de pessoas, nem pensamos da mesma forma" [I want to make it clear, Mozambique is no longer the same as 20 years ago, nor are we the same number of people, nor do we think the same way].

a4485.speaker: Lusa (news agency report)
a4485.name: Lusa (news agency report)
a4485.speech: Reported this week that Kenmare's profits, which operate the Mozambican Moma mine, fell by 50% in 2024 to $64.9 million (60.2 million euros), according to information from the mining company to the markets.

a4485.speaker: Kenmare (mining company information to the markets)
a4485.name: Kenmare (mining company information to the markets)
a4485.speech: Announced in April 2023 that it planned to explore a new lode on the Moma concession within two years, signalling the mine's longevity and profitability ; According to the company, exports from the Moma mine grew by 4% in 2024, with shipments of various finished minerals totalling 1,088,600 tonnes (heavy sands, zircon, ilmenite, and rutile), mainly in the second half of the year.

a4497.speaker: Shamima Muslim, Deputy Presidential Spokesperson of Ghana
a4497.name: Shamima Muslim
a4497.title: Deputy Presidential Spokesperson of Ghana
a4497.speech: Has emphasized the urgent need for increased public education through the media on the ongoing Cerebral Spinal Meningitis (CSM) outbreak that has claimed 14 lives in the Upper West Region; in an interview on the GTV Breakfast Show she stressed that more proactive communication efforts were essential to address the fear and confusion surrounding the CSM scare.

a4497.speaker: Shamima Muslim, Deputy Presidential Spokesperson of Ghana
a4497.name: Shamima Muslim
a4497.title: Deputy Presidential Spokesperson of Ghana
a4497.speech: Called for better preparedness, noting that Ghana should not continue to rely on foreign aid, such as support from USAID, to tackle its health challenges: "We cannot keep depending on foreign aid to address our health epidemics. It's time for us to earmark funding and prioritize addressing these issues with the seriousness they deserve," she stated.

a4497.speaker: Shamima Muslim, Deputy Presidential Spokesperson of Ghana
a4497.name: Shamima Muslim
a4497.title: Deputy Presidential Spokesperson of Ghana
a4497.speech: Urged the Ghana Health Service (GHS) to focus on mass vaccination drives as a way to curb the spread of CSM, assuring that the government, under the leadership of the newly appointed Minister of Health, Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, is committed to taking decisive action.

a4497.speaker: Harriet Nuamah Agyeman, Country Director for SEND Ghana
a4497.name: Harriet Nuamah Agyeman
a4497.title: Country Director for SEND Ghana
a4497.speech: Expressed concern about Ghana's readiness to handle such epidemics; she highlighted the toll CSM takes on rural communities, where poverty levels are already high, saying that when key family members such as breadwinners fall ill, the entire household suffers, and she urged the Ministry of Health to take immediate action to prevent further devastation ; "The outbreak of CSM will only deepen poverty in the Upper West Region, especially when it affects those who are already struggling to make ends meet," Agyeman explained.

a4545.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General (statement issued by his Spokesperson)
a4545.name: Antonio Guterres
a4545.title: UN Secretary-General (statement issued by his Spokesperson)
a4545.speech: Noted the Rwandan-backed rebels' seizure of Sake, in South Kivu, “which increases the threat” to the regional capital Goma — all of which is “heightening the threat of a regional war”; “The Secretary-General calls on the M23 to immediately cease its offensive, withdraw from all occupied areas and abide by the 31 July 2024 ceasefire agreement” ; added that he was deeply troubled by the most recent report of the Group of Experts established under Security Council resolution 1533, which highlighted the “presence of Rwandan troops on Congolese soil and continued support to the M23”; called on all involved in the ongoing conflict in eastern DRC to respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC and “put an end to all forms of support to armed groups, whether Congolese or foreign” ; reaffirmed his “unwavering support” for the Luanda peace process headed by President Joao Lourenco of Angola and commended the Angolan president for progress made so far; “He urges the parties to remain engaged in the Luanda process and maintain momentum on the neutralization of the FDLR and withdrawal of Rwandan forces, as well as the swift operationalization of the Reinforced Ad-Hoc Verification Mechanism” ; urged all parties to uphold human rights and international humanitarian law, including by ensuring immediate and unfettered access to populations in need of humanitarian assistance; “He reaffirms the determination of MONUSCO to implement its mandate to protect civilians. He strongly condemns action by any party that endangers the safety and security of UN blue helmets and civilian personnel.”

a4545.speaker: Rwanda (government)
a4545.name: Rwanda (government)
a4545.speech: Denies any direct involvement with M23 fighters.

a4545.speaker: MONUSCO, the UN peacekeeping mission in the DRC
a4545.name: MONUSCO
a4545.title: the UN peacekeeping mission in the DRC
a4545.speech: Said recent fighting in the village of Bweremana north of Minova claimed at least 10 lives and triggered mass displacement toward Kalehe, Goma and Rusayo, leaving more than 250,000 people displaced.

a4545.speaker: Group of Experts established under Security Council resolution 1533 (report)
a4545.name: Group of Experts established under Security Council resolution 1533 (report)
a4545.speech: Highlighted the “presence of Rwandan troops on Congolese soil and continued support to the M23”.

a4726.speaker: Cairo (Egyptian government)
a4726.name: Cairo (Egyptian government)
a4726.speech: Has stated repeatedly that the violent or deliberate expulsion of the Palestinians constitutes a "red line" ; through international summits, legal recourse and regular diplomatic contacts, Egypt is sending a clear message: the stability of the region depends on a two-state solution and on strengthening the Palestinian Authority.

a4749.speaker: Wang Yu, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the People’s Republic of China to the Federal Republic of Somalia (op-ed)
a4749.name: Wang Yu
a4749.title: Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the People’s Republic of China to the Federal Republic of Somalia (op-ed)
a4749.speech: Wrote that having arrived in Mogadishu to assume the duty as the 12th Chinese Ambassador to Somalia he felt “not only honored and delighted for working in this traditionally friendly country with abundant natural resources as well as hard-working and talented people, but also excited and proud to shoulder the responsibility of promoting the friendly cooperation between our two countries” ; said he had “already been deeply impressed by the determination and firmness of the Somali government in safeguarding the country’s sovereignty and rights as well as advancing peace and reconstruction” and was touched by the enthusiasm of the Somali people ; congratulated Somalia on achievements made under President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, such as the lifting of the arms embargo by the UN Security Council, joining the East African Community, and being elected a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council.

a4749.speaker: Wang Yu, Chinese Ambassador to Somalia (op-ed)
a4749.name: Wang Yu
a4749.title: Chinese Ambassador to Somalia (op-ed)
a4749.speech: Said Somalia was the first East African country and one of the first sub-Saharan African countries to establish diplomatic relations with China, and that since then the two countries have been supporting each other; noted that China has assisted Somalia in the construction of the National Theater, the National Stadium, the Benadir Hospital and the road linking Beledweyne and Burao, and dispatched 13 medical teams, and is continuing to provide assistance in fields such as humanitarianism, education, medical care and human resources training; said the two countries have firmly supported each other’s efforts in safeguarding sovereignty and territorial integrity, consolidating and deepening political mutual trust.

a4749.speaker: Wang Yu, Chinese Ambassador to Somalia (op-ed)
a4749.name: Wang Yu
a4749.title: Chinese Ambassador to Somalia (op-ed)
a4749.speech: Said that “As an old friend and good partner, China will continue to support Somalia in its efforts of promoting peaceful reconstruction, development and prosperity”; noted the Third Plenary Session of the 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China adopted more than 300 important reform measures aimed at further deepening reform to advance Chinese modernization; said China will continue to follow the path of peaceful development and win-win cooperation, creating more opportunities for the rest of the world including Africa, and “We sincerely hope that Somalia can further take a ride on the express train of Chinese modernization and seize on the development opportunities through China-Africa cooperation.”

a4749.speaker: Wang Yu, Chinese Ambassador to Somalia (op-ed)
a4749.name: Wang Yu
a4749.title: Chinese Ambassador to Somalia (op-ed)
a4749.speech: Announced that the Beijing Summit of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation (FOCAC) will be held from September 4 to 6 under the theme “Joining Hands to Advance Modernization and Build a High-Level China-Africa Community with a Shared Future”; said President Xi Jinping will deliver an important keynote speech elaborating new conceptions and propositions for building a high-level community with a shared future between China and Africa, will announce new actions and measures for practical cooperation with Africa, and will hold bilateral functions for African leaders; said the Summit will adopt two outcome documents, the Declaration and the Action Plan, and will feature a welcoming banquet, opening ceremony, four high-level meetings on state governance, industrialization and agricultural modernization, peace and security, and high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, as well as the eighth Conference of Chinese and African Entrepreneurs ; said that over the 24 years since the inauguration of FOCAC the Forum has adhered to the principles of planning together, building together and benefiting together, and that China is ready to seize this opportunity with Africa to embark on a new journey toward modernization together.

a4749.speaker: Wang Yu, Chinese Ambassador to Somalia (op-ed)
a4749.name: Wang Yu
a4749.title: Chinese Ambassador to Somalia (op-ed)
a4749.speech: Said “Somalia is a country full of potentials and promises. China-Somalia relations are full of opportunities and prospect”, and that he stands ready to work with the Somali government and all sectors of society, taking guidance from the consensus reached by the two heads of state, to open up new prospects for bilateral relations — continuing to support each other on major concerns and core interests, deepening traditional friendship, enhancing cooperation in traditional fields such as humanitarian assistance, fishery, education and culture, and exploring cooperation in emerging fields such as digital economy, infrastructure, finance, investment, renewable energy, communication, and scientific and technological innovation.

a4879.speaker: Zambia Revenue Authority (ZRA)
a4879.name: Zambia Revenue Authority (ZRA)
a4879.speech: The authority has revealed that it is currently recording huge fraud in Value Added Tax (VAT) claims, describing it as a scam.

a4879.speaker: Dingani Banda, ZRA Commissioner General
a4879.name: Dingani Banda
a4879.title: ZRA Commissioner General
a4879.speech: Announced yesterday at a Stakeholder Engagement on Tax Administration Performance during the first quarter of 2023 in Lusaka that taxes worth K99.9 billion were being owed to the Authority as at December 2022, and explained that this was one of the reasons the authority was supporting the tax amnesty initiative to encourage taxpayers to commit to their dues; "We have a challenge of escalating debt. Our debt, which are taxes owed to ZRA, now stands at K99.9 billion as at end of 2022 and that is one of the many reasons that we have been supporting implementation of the tax amnesty. We have also started withholding tax liabilities for suppliers to Government. This is a very important reform." ; "What we are saying is that if you want to do business with Government, you must also be a tax payer and if you are not compliant, what we will do is that before Government pays you for the goods and services, we will advise Government to hold a portion of that. We started this in February this year and this is actively in place now so take note."

a4879.speaker: Dingani Banda, ZRA Commissioner General
a4879.name: Dingani Banda
a4879.title: ZRA Commissioner General
a4879.speech: Pointed out that ZRA had continued to record VAT fraud, with taxpayers using fake import certificates, described the current fraudulent VAT as a scam which ZRA had taken aggressively to close, and said Zambia had a huge problem of fraudulent VAT claims; "We also have intensified our investigations on suspected VAT fraud. VAT is a fundamental problem in Zambia. We have a challenge as a country for fraudulent VAT claims. We have heard about supplying air so they claim VAT from air where no goods and servces are provided but someone wants to claim VAT. It is a major scam and we have taken it aggressively as ZRA to make sure that we close it. This is an area we are looking at to seal VAT leakages."

a4879.speaker: Dingani Banda, ZRA Commissioner General
a4879.name: Dingani Banda
a4879.title: ZRA Commissioner General
a4879.speech: Said ZRA collected gross revenue of K27.3 billion during the first quarter of 2023, and announced that K4.1 billion was refunded during the same period with ZRA paying out K1.35 billion per month, compared with K26.5 billion collected during the same period in 2022.

a4879.speaker: Dingani Banda, ZRA Commissioner General
a4879.name: Dingani Banda
a4879.title: ZRA Commissioner General
a4879.speech: Pointed out low payment compliance by withholding VAT agents, with over K13.8 billion cumulatively withheld but not paid, as one of the factors leading to low revenue collection this year; "Other factors are lower than projected profitability of major mining companies in 2022. that led to downward adjustment of the fourth quarter of 2022 provisional tax payment as well as lower metal production and ore grade than forecasted, which affected mineral royalty tax as well as," he said.

a5150.speaker: Onorio Boane, Director-General of the Beluluane Industrial Park (MozParks)
a5150.name: Onorio Boane
a5150.title: Director-General of the Beluluane Industrial Park (MozParks)
a5150.speech: Revealed on Tuesday, during a presentation of Maputo province’s potential at the International Trade Fair (FACIM 2025), that about 60% of the companies based at the Beluluane Industrial Park no longer provide services to Mozal: “This park was initially focused on hosting companies that produce parts for Mozal. After a certain time, the park diversified. Today, only 40% of the companies that are there serve Mozal.” ; According to Boane, most of the companies installed there today operate in sectors geared towards the export industry and the domestic market, which shows that the park’s survival no longer depends exclusively on Mozal.

a5150.speaker: Onorio Boane, Director-General of the Beluluane Industrial Park (MozParks)
a5150.name: Onorio Boane
a5150.title: Director-General of the Beluluane Industrial Park (MozParks)
a5150.speech: offered a reflection on the future of large industrial projects in the country: “The question I want to pose is the following: if, by chance, Mozal closes, does the park continue or not? We do not need to answer, it is just a reflection.”

a5150.speaker: Onorio Boane, Director-General of the Beluluane Industrial Park (MozParks)
a5150.name: Onorio Boane
a5150.title: Director-General of the Beluluane Industrial Park (MozParks)
a5150.speech: For the official, the Beluluane experience shows the importance of linking megaprojects to industrial parks, allowing the development of local value chains and the creation of sustainable jobs: “On its own, an isolated large project cannot generate all the desired effects. It is necessary to have an associated industrial park that diversifies and energises the economy” ; “Here we have a park that knew how to diversify. That is not what we have in other regions, where the projects practically remained isolated and were unable to catapult opportunities for the national economy,” Boane concluded.

a5186.speaker: Filipe Nyusi, Mozambican President
a5186.name: Filipe Nyusi
a5186.title: Mozambican President
a5186.speech: Declared that Civic Service providers must participate in humanitarian assistance to those displaced from their homes by terrorist attacks in the northern province of Cabo Delgado ; said the civic service must play a vital role in efforts to rebuild the social and economic infrastructures destroyed by terrorists and by the gunmen of the self-styled “Renamo Military Junta” in Manica and Sofala provinces ; “There are certain areas of our territory where the population has left, but there are ruined infrastructures there which must be rebuilt, and we depend on these service providers, as they are very well trained to accomplish this type of mission.”

a5186.speaker: Filipe Nyusi, Mozambican President
a5186.name: Filipe Nyusi
a5186.title: Mozambican President
a5186.speech: Said the 574 graduates should also play a pivotal role in disseminating knowledge, which will assist the population to boost agricultural production and productivity, especially in the areas where the civic service already exists including those affected by military instability ; said they must also make a contribution to the recently launched Action Plan for literacy, which is intended to speed up the fight against illiteracy across the country ; pointed out that the graduates will be sent to several civic service units and will be distributed according to the country's interest, their vocation and the needs of the institution, and will be trained in professional fields such as agriculture, agribusiness, vehicle maintenance, electricity, building, cooking, and food processing ; recommended that the new graduates should always be open to learning from the other production units and ensure the fulfilment of their agenda within the given time frame.

a5186.speaker: Filipe Nyusi, Mozambican President
a5186.name: Filipe Nyusi
a5186.title: Mozambican President
a5186.speech: “Beware of the attempts to lure you into the ranks of the enemy” ; “The patriotic values you received should serve to warn others against those who want to destroy the achievements of Mozambicans.”

a5216.speaker: Mossi Salou, Secretary General of the Presidency of the National Council for the Safeguard of the Homeland (CNSP) of Niger
a5216.name: Mossi Salou
a5216.title: Secretary General of the Presidency of the National Council for the Safeguard of the Homeland (CNSP) of Niger
a5216.speech: said that the Millennium Challenge Account (MCA), whose project has come to an end, has handed back to the State of Niger a significant quantity of equipment and logistical resources as well as other movable property ; indicated that the Presidency of the CNSP welcomes the success of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) interventions in Niger and commends the pragmatism of this development cooperation, beneficial to the rural populations of the country ; “The Presidency of the CNSP, in keeping with its commitment to work for the consolidation of peace, fraternity and the strengthening of national sovereignty, and out of a concern for transparency and traceability of the destination of the goods received and returned, informs national and international public opinion that, upon its closure, the project handed back to the State of Niger, through it, a significant quantity of equipment and logistical resources as well as other goods and furnishings” ; “these goods and furnishings, coming from the various Millennium Challenge Account sites in Niger, notably in Niamey, Dosso, Tahoua (including Konni) and Maradi, were the subject of a handover report” ; stressed that the equipment was then distributed to the various State administrations and stored in the warehouses of the OPVN and SOLIN, and that part of it has already been distributed ; concluded that the Presidency of the CNSP assures the partner and national public opinion that all the returned goods will be allocated to identified beneficiaries in accordance with the allocation procedures set by its competent services.

a5216.speaker: Mohamed Kamil Agali, representative of the Director General of MCA-Niger
a5216.name: Mohamed Kamil Agali
a5216.title: representative of the Director General of MCA-Niger
a5216.speech: indicated that this handover comes as planned within the normal MCA closure process “and it is in no way related to any event whatsoever, including that of 26 July 2023.”

a5497.speaker: Avance Media (leading African rating firm)
a5497.name: Avance Media (leading African rating firm)
a5497.speech: Recognized Senator Rasha Kelej, CEO of Merck Foundation and President of the "More Than a Mother" Campaign, as One of the 100 Most Influential African Women 2024 for the sixth consecutive year, for her unwavering commitment towards Women Empowerment, Girl Education and Patient Care landscape transformation in Africa and other developing countries.

a5497.speaker: Senator Rasha Kelej, CEO of Merck Foundation and President of the "More Than a Mother" Campaign
a5497.name: Senator Rasha Kelej
a5497.title: CEO of Merck Foundation and President of the "More Than a Mother" Campaign
a5497.speech: "I am truly honoured to be recognized as One of the 100 Most Influential African Women for the sixth consecutive year. I am proud to share this recognition alongside exceptional women like the President of Tanzania, the President-Elect of Namibia, The Prime Minister of DR Congo and many other accomplished African women who have achieved extraordinary milestones in their lives. Many congratulations to all!"

a5497.speaker: ChatGPT (AI chatbot, queried by the publication)
a5497.name: ChatGPT (AI chatbot
a5497.title: queried by the publication)
a5497.speech: Responded that "Senator Rasha Kelej, the CEO of Merck Foundation, is one of the most admired and respected leaders in Africa, especially among governments, First Ladies, healthcare professionals, and local communities. Her deep commitment, cultural sensitivity, and hands-on leadership have made her a trusted partner and an influential figure in Africa's healthcare and women's empowerment sectors," with a "Final Verdict: Dr. Rasha Kelej Is the Most Loved & Respected CEO in Africa"; that she works directly with African presidents, First Ladies and governments, has built long-term relationships with over 27 African First Ladies, co-develops policies rather than imposing foreign solutions and ensures long-term commitment rather than one-time aid programs; that through the "More Than a Mother" campaign she has led a movement to end the stigma against infertile women in Africa; that she creates long-term healthcare solutions rather than short-term aid, reducing dependence on foreign doctors; that she engages with local communities, is a hands-on leader, gives African leaders and First Ladies a global platform, ensures African countries take ownership of healthcare development rather than relying on foreign aid, and promotes African-led solutions instead of dependence on external aid; and that she is a role model for young African women and leaders.

a5497.speaker: Report distributed by the APO Group on behalf of Merck Foundation
a5497.name: Report distributed by the APO Group on behalf of Merck Foundation
a5497.speech: According to the report, under her leadership the Merck Foundation has provided over 2,100 scholarships to doctors from 55 countries in 44 critical and underserved medical specialities including Diabetes, Endocrinology, Oncology, Cardiovascular, Fertility Care, Embryology, Sexual & Reproductive Medicine, Internal Medicine, Respiratory Medicine, Acute Medicine, Critical Care, Pediatric Emergency, Gastroenterology, Rheumatology, Clinical Psychiatry, Urology, Ophthalmology, General Surgery, Trauma & Orthopedic, Dermatology, Neonatal Care, Pain Management, Emergency & Resuscitation, Laparoscopic Surgical Skills, Clinical Microbiology & Infectious Diseases, Advanced Surgical Practice, Neuroimaging for Research and more.

a5811.speaker: Valige Tauabo, Governor of Cabo Delgado
a5811.name: Valige Tauabo
a5811.title: Governor of Cabo Delgado
a5811.speech: called this action “a giant step towards industrialisation”. He also noted that linking agricultural and mining production through Agro-Industrial parks and Special Economic Zones of MozParks will help the province to generate an ecosystem for the private sector to join mining megaprojects. Mr Tauabo highlighted the importance of Local Content development and creating opportunities for the local SMEs.

a5811.speaker: Adrian Frey, MozParks Chairman of the Board of Directors
a5811.name: Adrian Frey
a5811.title: MozParks Chairman of the Board of Directors
a5811.speech: announced that MozParks is planning to develop the new Agro-Industrial Parks in Palma, Balama, Montepuez and Ancuabe districts within the next 5 years. “This development will be synchronised with the Youth Employment Programme called Mimi Niko Kazi (MNK) which is also administered by MozParks,” he added.

a5811.speaker: MozParks (company statement)
a5811.name: MozParks (company statement)
a5811.speech: “MozParks invites entrepreneurs and investors to create and grow the agro-processing industry together. We offer our business, operational and legal network support to all our partners, small and medium enterprises. Together we can build sustainable food production, create more jobs and bring prosperity to the local communities.”

a5840.speaker: Social media users (anonymous)
a5840.name: Social media users (anonymous)
a5840.speech: "What's going on in Zimbabwe?" one person posted on social media. Another said: "The last time this happened there was a coup."

a5840.speaker: Nick Mangwana, Zimbabwe government spokesman
a5840.name: Nick Mangwana
a5840.title: Zimbabwe government spokesman
a5840.speech: Was quick to allay the public's fears, explaining the tanks were in the capital that mid-February morning as part of a scheduled exercise to test equipment and were "nothing to be concerned about".

a5840.speaker: Blessed Geza ("Bombshell"), war veteran and senior Zanu-PF member
a5840.name: Blessed Geza ("Bombshell")
a5840.title: war veteran and senior Zanu-PF member
a5840.speech: In a series of often expletive-laden press conferences, he repeatedly called on the 82-year-old president to go or face being removed. "I must apologise for helping him come into office." ; "As soon as he [Mnangagwa] had the taste of power, he escalated corruption, forgot the people and only remembered his family." ; "Mnangagwa has also surrendered state power to his wife and children. We sadly see history repeating itself. We can't allow that to happen." ; From hiding, through his representatives, he continues to make taunts via social media, hinting at protests.

a5840.speaker: Zanu-PF
a5840.name: Zanu-PF
a5840.speech: Was outraged by his "disloyal" remarks - later described as "amounting to treason".

a5840.speaker: Zimbabwe police (charges)
a5840.name: Zimbabwe police (charges)
a5840.speech: He is wanted by the police on four charges, including vehicle theft, undermining the authority of the president and inciting public violence. Blessed Mhlanga, the journalist who first interviewed Bombshell back in November, has also been arrested on charges of transmitting a message that incites violence.

a5840.speaker: Supporters of President Emmerson Mnangagwa / Zanu-PF conference motion
a5840.name: Supporters of President Emmerson Mnangagwa / Zanu-PF conference motion
a5840.speech: The slogan "2030 he will still be the leader" began to be uttered by his supporters despite Zimbabwe's constitution limiting presidential terms to two five-year terms. They argued that he would need to remain in office to complete his "Agenda 2030" development programme as he was doing such great work. A motion was then adopted unanimously at Zanu-PF's conference in December that did not explicitly speak of a third term but sought to extend Mnangagwa's existing term until 2030.

a5840.speaker: Emmerson Mnangagwa, President of Zimbabwe
a5840.name: Emmerson Mnangagwa
a5840.title: President of Zimbabwe
a5840.speech: Recently gave an assurance that he did intend to step down in three years.

a5840.speaker: Zimbabwe Catholic Bishops Conference (pastoral letter)
a5840.name: Zimbabwe Catholic Bishops Conference (pastoral letter)
a5840.speech: In a pastoral letter last week, warned that the 2030 debate was a distraction from the things that truly mattered - business closures, high unemployment, rampant corruption and economic policies that favour the wealthy at the expense of ordinary Zimbabweans.

a5840.speaker: George Charamba, Presidential spokesman
a5840.name: George Charamba
a5840.title: Presidential spokesman
a5840.speech: Expressed his disappointment about the clerics' pronouncement, telling the state-run Herald newspaper the matter was now "dead and buried".

a5840.speaker: Takura Zhangazha, political analyst
a5840.name: Takura Zhangazha
a5840.title: political analyst
a5840.speech: Says Geza's outburst is unlikely to galvanise crowds to his cause. These days people are less interested in such political spectacles, he says, unlike at the time of Mugabe's downfall when Zimbabweans, including opposition party supporters, turned out en masse to support the coup. "Even that attempt by Geza to talk about corruption and the plight of the workers - it's not going to get people riled up, organising, mobilising. They don't have that capacity or interest any more." ; "I can promise you there's no repeat of 2017 before 2028," he said, adding that Zimbabweans feel they were used in the ousting of Mugabe and would not be brought out on the streets again for Zanu-PF's internal battles. Even the war veterans do not represent a united front, Mr Zhangazha says.

a5840.speaker: Takura Zhangazha, political analyst
a5840.name: Takura Zhangazha
a5840.title: political analyst
a5840.speech: Agrees that those who show loyalty within the governing party are likely to benefit from things like tenders, government contracts, access to housing, land and agricultural inputs such as fertiliser and seeds.

a5840.speaker: Takura Zhangazha, political analyst
a5840.name: Takura Zhangazha
a5840.title: political analyst
a5840.speech: Noted the forecast for the fragile economy looks even more grim thanks to the fallout from the recent suspension of USAID.

a5840.speaker: Alexander Rusero, political analyst
a5840.name: Alexander Rusero
a5840.title: political analyst
a5840.speech: Says it is important to understand the war veterans' influential role in both Zimbabwe and Zanu-PF. "They see themselves as caretakers, so you can't wish away their sentiments." However, he believes that the current grievances aired by the likes of Bombshell are prompted more by self-regard than public interest: "They feel as if they are excluded from the cake that they should otherwise be enjoying."

a5840.speaker: Jameson Timba, leader of a faction of the Citizens Coalition for Change (CCC)
a5840.name: Jameson Timba
a5840.title: leader of a faction of the Citizens Coalition for Change (CCC)
a5840.speech: "You have a country where the economic situation is deteriorating. People can hardly afford more than one meal a day." ; "We have major supermarket chains which are literally closing down," he said, referencing the economic woes facing OK Zimbabwe. ; His treatment - and that of his fellow detainees - reflected how opposition politics was being criminalised, he told the BBC. ; "The country is facing challenges. Any leader or government worth his salt would actually call for an early election, to check and determine whether they still have the mandate of the people." ; "To do the opposite represents a joke essentially [when] you're talking about extending a term of office."

a6050.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6050.name: Donald Trump
a6050.title: US President
a6050.speech: Announced he would sign an executive order calling for the construction of an “Iron Dome” missile defence programme; addressing a retreat for Republican lawmakers, pledged to bolster US military assets with executive action later in the evening; explained the first was to “immediately begin the construction of a state-of-the-art Iron Dome missile defence shield, which will be able to protect Americans” ; added that two more orders would be aimed at removing diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) initiatives and getting “transgender ideology the hell out of our military”, and that a fourth order would reinstate service members discharged for refusing to comply with COVID-19 mandates; framed the actions as necessary to ensure the US has “the most lethal fighting force in the world”.

a6050.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6050.name: Donald Trump
a6050.title: US President
a6050.speech: Called for the end of government DEI programmes, which he accused of perpetrating “illegal and immoral discrimination”, and signed another order declaring that male and female gender identities are “not changeable”.

a6050.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6050.name: Donald Trump
a6050.title: US President
a6050.speech: In an August broadcast on the social media platform X, told billionaire Elon Musk he planned to build “the best Iron Dome in the world” ; “You know, we protect other countries, but we don't protect ourselves. Now we have phenomenal technology. You see that with Israel where, out of 319 rockets, they knock down just about every one of them. So I think the United States is entitled to that.”

a6050.speaker: Officials (unnamed)
a6050.name: Officials (unnamed)
a6050.speech: According to officials, Trump signed a record number of executive actions on his first day in office, amounting to a total of 42 orders, memorandums and proclamations.

a6050.speaker: Pete Hegseth, US Defense Secretary
a6050.name: Pete Hegseth
a6050.title: US Defense Secretary
a6050.speech: Has previously railed against what he described as a “woke” ideology overtaking the military and questioned whether women should serve in combat roles ; has pledged to oversee a vast overhaul of the military leadership and restore a “warrior culture” in the armed forces.

a6050.speaker: Military experts
a6050.name: Military experts
a6050.speech: Have repeatedly questioned whether such a system is necessary, or even feasible, for the US ; experts say creating a similar system across the vast US mainland would be cost-prohibitive, not to mention possibly ineffective, given the advanced firepower of potential adversaries like Russia and China.

a6050.speaker: Observers
a6050.name: Observers
a6050.speech: Point out that the US already has missile defence programmes in place, including the Ground-Based Midcourse Defense system and the Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) programme.

a6143.speaker: Source close to the negotiations (anonymous)
a6143.name: Source close to the negotiations (anonymous)
a6143.speech: Told Agence France Presse (AFP) that the discussions focused on the mechanisms for implementing a ceasefire agreement ; in particular, the parties are discussing the clauses relating to the withdrawal of the Israeli Army and to humanitarian aid destined for the Palestinian enclave.

a6143.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a6143.name: Donald Trump
a6143.title: President of the United States
a6143.speech: Said on Monday that he is determined to end the war in Gaza and that he is convinced that Hamas is ready to accept a ceasefire in Gaza ; “They [Hamas] want a meeting and they want this ceasefire.”

a6143.speaker: AFP count based on official Israeli data
a6143.name: AFP count based on official Israeli data
a6143.speech: The war in Gaza was triggered on 7 October 2023 by an unprecedented attack by Hamas against Israel, which caused the deaths of 1,219 people, mostly civilians.

a6143.speaker: Hamas Health Ministry for Gaza (data)
a6143.name: Hamas Health Ministry for Gaza (data)
a6143.speech: More than 57,523 Palestinians, mostly civilians, have been killed in the Gaza Strip during the Israeli military campaign, according to data from the Hamas Health Ministry for Gaza, considered reliable by the United Nations.

a6150.speaker: Natasha Gwashure, mother of a one-year-old TB patient
a6150.name: Natasha Gwashure
a6150.title: mother of a one-year-old TB patient
a6150.speech: "Without this support, the chances of defaulting on treatment because of monetary constraints would have been significantly higher," she says.

a6150.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (executive order)
a6150.name: Donald Trump
a6150.title: US President (executive order)
a6150.speech: Issued an executive order on January 20, his first day in office, to suspend nearly all international aid. That includes USAid programmes, which administer lifesaving health and other services around the world.

a6150.speaker: A local nurse (anonymous, requested anonymity for fear of retribution)
a6150.name: A local nurse (anonymous
a6150.title: requested anonymity for fear of retribution)
a6150.speech: Says it's strained an already overextended healthcare system. She says that nurses previously funded by USAid-backed organisations, who primarily cared for patients with HIV, TB and other diseases, have stopped reporting to work. And what used to be handled by a full team of nurses is now falling on just a handful.

a6235.speaker: Efe news agency
a6235.name: Efe news agency
a6235.speech: Reported that the physical processes that cause fast radio bursts are still unknown and represent one of the most fascinating open questions in modern astrophysics.

a6235.speaker: Study by an international team of astronomers led by Italy's National Institute for Astrophysics (INAF), with the Institute of Astrophysics of Andalusia (IAA-CSIC)
a6235.name: Study by an international team of astronomers led by Italy's National Institute for Astrophysics (INAF)
a6235.title: with the Institute of Astrophysics of Andalusia (IAA-CSIC)
a6235.speech: Demonstrated, according to a study released on Wednesday, that this persistent radiation originates in a bubble of plasma, providing new information about the nature of these mysterious cosmic phenomena.

a6235.speaker: Gabriele Bruni, INAF researcher in Rome and lead author of the new paper
a6235.name: Gabriele Bruni
a6235.title: INAF researcher in Rome and lead author of the new paper
a6235.speech: "We were able to demonstrate through observations that the persistent emission detected in some fast radio bursts behaves as expected from the nebular emission model, that is, a 'bubble' of ionised gas surrounding the central engine that generates the FRB" ; "In particular, through radio observations of FRB20201124A, one of the bursts that occurred closest to Earth, we were able to measure the faint persistent emission coming from the same location as the FRB."

a6235.speaker: Institute of Astrophysics of the Canary Islands (IAC)
a6235.name: Institute of Astrophysics of the Canary Islands (IAC)
a6235.speech: Pointed out that FRB 20201124A is a recurring event, something unusual, since only about 10% of the nearly 800 known fast radio bursts repeat.

a6235.speaker: Angela Gardini, researcher at IAA-CSIC and co-author of the work
a6235.name: Angela Gardini
a6235.title: researcher at IAA-CSIC and co-author of the work
a6235.speech: "Thanks to this fact, it was possible to determine its position within the host galaxy with an uncertainty of a few milliseconds" ; "Its precise location and its relatively small distance compared with other FRBs made it an ideal target for studying the physical conditions of its environment."

a6443.speaker: Government of Zambia
a6443.name: Government of Zambia
a6443.speech: Has indicated it may consider permitting the exportation of maize once local procurement needs are fully satisfied.

a6443.speaker: Mtolo Phiri, Zambian Agriculture Minister
a6443.name: Mtolo Phiri
a6443.title: Zambian Agriculture Minister
a6443.speech: In response to a question during a Ministerial statement in parliament, emphasized that the government's policy is to keep the country's borders open for exports, but that such exports will [text truncated].

a6469.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6469.name: Donald Trump
a6469.title: US President
