a6469.speech: Claimed on Thursday, without formal evidence, that billions of dollars had been stolen from USAID in order to fund favourable media coverage for his opponents: “It looks like billions of dollars have been stolen at USAID, and other agencies, much of it going to the fake news media as a ‘payoff’ for creating good stories about the Democrats,” he said in a message published on social media.

a6469.speaker: Trump administration
a6469.name: Trump administration
a6469.speech: Announced on Monday that it would place on leave all employees directly hired by USAID worldwide and recall thousands of people working abroad, after the president in January ordered a freeze on most US foreign aid.

a6469.speaker: Donald Trump and his advisers
a6469.name: Donald Trump and his advisers
a6469.speech: Say they want to ensure that the billions of dollars of American aid, including humanitarian aid, comply with his “America First” policy.

a6469.speaker: Elon Musk, billionaire tasked with cutting USAID staff
a6469.name: Elon Musk
a6469.title: billionaire tasked with cutting USAID staff
a6469.speech: Has accused USAID of being a criminal organisation.

a6519.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP), latest report on the humanitarian crisis
a6519.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a6519.title: latest report on the humanitarian crisis
a6519.speech: Reveals that the WFP has resumed the delivery of full humanitarian food assistance to host families and displaced persons in Cabo Delgado, northern Mozambique, after aid packages delivered to each family had been reduced to 39% of daily energy needs since July 2021 due to a lack of funds; during the month of January, WFP helped 980,000 people in Cabo Delgado, Nampula and Niassa.

a6519.speaker: Famine Early Warning Systems Network (FEWS NET), document released on Monday
a6519.name: Famine Early Warning Systems Network (FEWS NET)
a6519.title: document released on Monday
a6519.speech: Announces that “Full rations are expected to be distributed from January to March,” adding that the plan is subject to change according to the availability of additional resources and the redirection of priorities, with a potential pipeline break in April due to a lack of funds ; reports that “sporadic attacks by scattered groups of insurgents are reigniting fear” among the population, a scenario that “limits [the] active participation in the agricultural season”; that a new area of food ‘stress' has emerged in Mecula, in Niassa province, due to attacks that forced the flight of 3,700 inhabitants; that across Mozambique most poor households are experiencing None (IPC Phase 1) or Stressed (IPC Phase 2) outcomes, with conflict-affected areas of Cabo Delgado likely facing Crisis (IPC Phase 3); that Moderate Tropical Storm Ana made landfall in Nampula province on 24 January 2022 causing widespread flooding; that heavy rainfall in South Africa and Eswatini resulted in the opening of dam gates and flood alert levels along the Maputo, Incomáti and Umbelúzi rivers, with up to 15 percent of planted areas in several Maputo province districts possibly impacted; that international and regional forecasts indicate La Niña conditions are likely to continue through March-May 2022 and rainfall for January to March 2022 is expected to be below average in southern and eastern Mozambique; and that from November to December 2021 maize grain prices had a mixed trend across markets.

a6519.speaker: INGD (preliminary assessments)
a6519.name: INGD (preliminary assessments)
a6519.speech: As of 28 January 2022, preliminary assessments by the INGD indicate over 126,000 people have been affected, along with the destruction of more than 5,700 homes, 543 classrooms, 30 health facilities, 45 roads, and the flooding of over 37,900 hectares of cropland.

a6519.speaker: Mozambican authorities
a6519.name: Mozambican authorities
a6519.speech: Have attributed the attacks that forced the flight of 3,700 inhabitants of Mecula, Niassa province, to insurgents fleeing Cabo Delgado.

a6625.speaker: Roberto Albino, Mozambican Minister of Agriculture, Environment and Fisheries
a6625.name: Roberto Albino
a6625.title: Mozambican Minister of Agriculture, Environment and Fisheries
a6625.speech: Says it is necessary to strengthen the private sector, giving it resources and independence to produce enough to meet demand, and states that his sector will work hard to combat hunger in the country, with the bet being on small and medium-sized enterprises: “We would like to make clear that our bet will be entirely centred on catapulting the private sector. We want to stimulate a demand-based growth approach, so that micro, small and medium-scale entrepreneurs are at the forefront of the process and can grow sustainably.”

a6625.speaker: Roberto Albino, Mozambican Minister of Agriculture, Environment and Fisheries
a6625.name: Roberto Albino
a6625.title: Mozambican Minister of Agriculture, Environment and Fisheries
a6625.speech: Admits that it is necessary to stop depending on foreign aid: “The approach of waiting only for subsidies or for foreign direct investment has proved increasingly unsustainable. We have wasted time by limiting ourselves to postponing our progress. We must bet on the national private sector, providing it with an attractive and secure business environment, facilitating its operation without barriers.”

a6625.speaker: Roberto Albino, Mozambican Minister of Agriculture, Environment and Fisheries
a6625.name: Roberto Albino
a6625.title: Mozambican Minister of Agriculture, Environment and Fisheries
a6625.speech: States that it is necessary to stop making excuses and to work tirelessly to respond to the needs of the population: “The Mozambican people expect from us ever greater access to food, and not excuses and civic postponements. Only with hard work, adequate institutional policies and interventions in rural and urban development can we ensure ever-increasing access to food for our population. We also need to guarantee the supply of raw material to our industry, as a decisive sector of our agrarian and fisheries sector.”

a6767.speaker: Hope Uzodimma, Governor of Imo State
a6767.name: Hope Uzodimma
a6767.title: Governor of Imo State
a6767.speech: Told media executives, including executive members of the Nigerian Guild of Editors, to freely go round the state to see what his government had done: "Take time to move around the state and see for yourselves, the progress we have made in building Imo into a model of excellence. As you do, you will notice that the flyover at Assumpta Roundabout was not there when last you were here. You will also see that the World-Class International Conference Centre at Orlu Road junction has since been completed." ; "But above all, I urge you to interact with the management of the Orashi Electricity Company, so that you can be well appraised of how far we have gone in our determination, to provide 24/7 electricity across all 27 local government areas of the state in the coming months." ; "I am confident that by the time you conclude your visit, you will agree with us that a new Imo is truly on the rise."

a6767.speaker: Chibuzo Agwuamba, engineer handling the Mgbe/Umuchima erosion site project
a6767.name: Chibuzo Agwuamba
a6767.title: engineer handling the Mgbe/Umuchima erosion site project
a6767.speech: Told media executives that the double lane and bridge would be completed in no time, adding that the Orashi River, which was diverted to enable construction work, would soon flow naturally, like before.

a6767.speaker: Eze Anaba, President of the Nigerian Guild of Editors
a6767.name: Eze Anaba
a6767.title: President of the Nigerian Guild of Editors
a6767.speech: "The most impressive of the projects that I saw was the road linking the former governor's place. It is very impressive. The narrative was that, it is a Federal Road that had been abandoned for a while, but it's the people of the state that use the road. A significant part of the state had been cut off; so the fact that the governor deemed it fit to link the two together is highly commendable. I even learnt that one can connect Anambra, using the road and it makes it more impressive."

a6767.speaker: Eze Anaba, President of the Nigerian Guild of Editors
a6767.name: Eze Anaba
a6767.title: President of the Nigerian Guild of Editors
a6767.speech: "I want to congratulate the governor because, that's what is called good governance. If people are able to move about, it will encourage commerce, improve well-being and that's what governance is all about, that's what we call democracy, to let people enjoy the dividends of democracy." ; "We saw the flyover, too, it's another significant project. On the international conference centre, we had earlier seen what was constructed in the past, when the Guild came to Owerri two years ago for our biennial convention. But this is in a class of its own. The Emmanuel Iwuanyanwu International Conference is excellent. It will attract a lot of business and revenue to the state. A whole lot of business can be done; a whole industry can open up. Conferences will hold, and you will see things beginning to happen for good. It's quite impressive."

a6767.speaker: Eze Anaba, President of the Nigerian Guild of Editors
a6767.name: Eze Anaba
a6767.title: President of the Nigerian Guild of Editors
a6767.speech: Described the fallacy of Imo State being an insecurity destination as politics, saying though he was unqualified to speak on the issue having been in the state for just two days, "with what I've seen so far, and where I've been, people are going about their business without fears. My prayer is that peace is for everybody, let the people breathe." ; "Let there be peace in the South East, so that people can live, so that development can come. We should not escalate the fear, that the South East is unlivable. It's not good for anybody. My plea is, let there be peace in the South East."

a6767.speaker: Eze Anaba, President of the Nigerian Guild of Editors
a6767.name: Eze Anaba
a6767.title: President of the Nigerian Guild of Editors
a6767.speech: On road infrastructure, posited that the governor has done excellently well on road construction, adding that the worst democracy is far better than the best military administration: "If a civilian government decides to work, just the way Governor Uzodimma is working, the people will benefit, and in Imo State, the people are benefitting. So, I can only encourage the governor to keep it up."

a6767.speaker: Hope Uzodimma, Governor of Imo State
a6767.name: Hope Uzodimma
a6767.title: Governor of Imo State
a6767.speech: Said in his "State of the State Address" to members of the Imo House of Assembly and Imo indigenes on Tuesday, June 24, 2025: "When I assume office, I was immediately confronted with two pressing issues: widespread infrastructure decay, and the near-total breakdown of state institutions." ; "Most roads were either, impassable or outright death traps. Governance was paralyzed. The civil service, often referred to as the engine room of government, had lost both its form and function. Even, the Government House had been reduced to a laughable caricature, with official business often conducted in Bush Bars or Guest Houses." ; "We began our rebuilding efforts with the civil service and critical road infrastructure within the Owerri Capital City. The choice was deliberate. A functional civil service is the backbone of good governance, and motorable roads are essential for commerce, public mobility and adminstrative efficiency."

a6767.speaker: Hope Uzodimma, Governor of Imo State
a6767.name: Hope Uzodimma
a6767.title: Governor of Imo State
a6767.speech: Told the Assembly members "Our commitment to infrastructure remains resolute", revealing that his administration has constructed more roads than all previous administrations since 1999 combined and that Imo now boasts one of the most extensive and impactful road networks in Nigeria: "To date, we have completed over 129 roads across the state. In the past 18 months alone; we delivered 37 brand new roads, an iconic edifice, International Conference Centre and befitting Government House Annex, Orlu." ; "We also have the Assumpta Flyover and the new Concorde-Hilton Hotel as landmark legacy projects."

a6767.speaker: Hope Uzodimma, Governor of Imo State
a6767.name: Hope Uzodimma
a6767.title: Governor of Imo State
a6767.speech: Recently announced a minimum wage of N104,000 for state workers.

a6870.speaker: Melkiory Ngido, Barrick's Country Manager (Tanzania)
a6870.name: Melkiory Ngido
a6870.title: Barrick's Country Manager (Tanzania)
a6870.speech: unveiled that Twiga Minerals, a partnership between Barrick Gold Corporation and Tanzania, contributes 51 per cent of the country's mining sector revenue ; “The partnership through Twiga Minerals showcases how the government can effectively collaborate with the private sector for the benefit of the nation, as evidenced by the various successes since its establishment.” ; said this makes Barrick the leading contributor to the national revenue through taxes and other government fees in the mining sector, thus supporting the country's economic growth ; explained that in addition to contributing to the national revenue, the partnership has also created employment opportunities for Tanzanians, driven significant social projects through the Corporate Social Responsibility policy, particularly in sectors like roads, healthcare, water and education, and boosted the local economy by supporting local suppliers ; “A point of pride is that the majority of workers at Barrick and Twiga mines are locals and the operations are led by Tanzanians.”

a6870.speaker: Melkiory Ngido, Barrick's Country Manager (Tanzania)
a6870.name: Melkiory Ngido
a6870.title: Barrick's Country Manager (Tanzania)
a6870.speech: discussed how Barrick is collaborating with the government on a unique project aimed at enhancing the future of education in the country — the ‘Barrick-Twiga Future Forward Education’ — focused on improving the infrastructure of public secondary schools, particularly at the advanced level, to increase the number of students who can continue their education despite infrastructure challenges, while ensuring they study in conducive environments.

a6870.speaker: Tanzania Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (TEITI) latest report
a6870.name: Tanzania Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (TEITI) latest report
a6870.speech: According to the latest report from TEITI, this partnership demonstrates how public-private partnerships can achieve major successes, citing the 51 per cent current revenue contribution leading others in the mining sector.

a6967.speaker: Amilcar Cabral (lyrics of "Esta e a nossa patria amada", quoted)
a6967.name: Amilcar Cabral (lyrics of "Esta e a nossa patria amada"
a6967.title: quoted)
a6967.speech: "Sun, sweat, the green and the sea, / centuries of pain and hope; / this is the land of our forefathers! ... Long live the glorious homeland! / The banner of struggle has flowered in the skies. / Forward, against the foreign yoke! / We shall build / in the immortal homeland / peace and progress!"

a6967.speaker: Silva and Lopes (lyrics of the "Hino da Liberdade" / Hymn of Liberty, quoted)
a6967.name: Silva and Lopes (lyrics of the "Hino da Liberdade" / Hymn of Liberty
a6967.title: quoted)
a6967.speech: "Sing, brother / sing, my brother / for freedom is a hymn / and man is certainty ... Sentinel of seas and persevering winds / between the stars and the Atlantic / sing the song of freedom."

a6967.speaker: Aristotle
a6967.name: Aristotle
a6967.speech: The Stagirite says that "man is by nature a political animal."

a6967.speaker: Plato
a6967.name: Plato
a6967.speech: Replies with the timeless warning: "the punishment of the good who abstain from politics is to be governed by the wicked."

a6967.speaker: "O Guerreiro" (The Warrior)
a6967.name: "O Guerreiro" (The Warrior)
a6967.speech: Asks, with the weight of the years and of constitutional frustrations: was it for this that the flags of independence/democracy were raised?

a6967.speaker: Zeze de Nha Reinalda, singer
a6967.name: Zeze de Nha Reinalda
a6967.title: singer
a6967.speech: Sang: "There is nobody who loves my land more than I do, just give me a plot of land in Prainha and guarantee my wife a job at TACV."

a6967.speaker: Tavares (lyrics of "Nos Cabo Verde di speranca", quoted)
a6967.name: Tavares (lyrics of "Nos Cabo Verde di speranca"
a6967.title: quoted)
a6967.speech: "Our Cabo Verde of hope (...); but hope is not just sitting and waiting; let us not leave everything for the State to do (...); let us come together to build our land; each one of us is a Cabral (...); our Cabo Verde lives only on hope; hope that one day we will live properly; hope that one day we may sow, harvest and eat (...); how long will hope go on? On what day will our Cabo turn Verde [green]?"

a7206.speaker: Participants in the roundtable discussion on gender based violence in Gombe State
a7206.name: Participants in the roundtable discussion on gender based violence in Gombe State
a7206.speech: Believe that there are uncountable number of such violations, particularly rape and sexual abuse incidents involving girls and in some cases boys, which had gradually become a norm to these victims; lamented the true life stories and many untold ones happening in many parts of the State, including school age girls sent on hawking being lured and sexually violated by adults, and noted that in some instances threats to life are issued by perpetrators or other family members to protect the family name.

a7206.speaker: Stakeholders that participated in the discussion
a7206.name: Stakeholders that participated in the discussion
a7206.speech: Called for enhanced support for survivors, policy reforms and increased awareness to address the negative growing trend.

a7206.speaker: Participants in the discussion (traditional rulers, civil society organisations, faith based groups, government officials)
a7206.name: Participants in the discussion (traditional rulers
a7206.title: civil society organisations, faith based groups, government officials)
a7206.speech: Emphasized the need to break the culture of silence by exposing perpetrators and strengthening mechanisms for survivors ; called for reviving referral pathways to provide safe spaces for survivors and establishment of gender desks offices across ministries to improve institutional responses to GBV ; pledged their commitment towards creating awareness, pushing for systematic change and ensuring that survivors receive the care they deserve.

a7206.speaker: Chabiyada Eli, Gender and Social Inclusion Coordinator of the USAID Nigeria State Accountability, Transparency and Effectiveness (State2State) programme
a7206.name: Chabiyada Eli
a7206.title: Gender and Social Inclusion Coordinator of the USAID Nigeria State Accountability, Transparency and Effectiveness (State2State) programme
a7206.speech: Pointed out during her presentation that violence against women and girls continue to impede equality, development and peace; according to her, one in every three women experience violence, a statistic that has refused to change over the years: "This persistent issue has continue to hinder the participation of women and girls at all levels of governance" ; called on Government, CSO's, private sector stakeholders and influencers to intensify efforts towards eliminating GBV and stressed the need for collective action to build a safer society.

a7505.speaker: Godswill Akpabio, Senate President of Nigeria
a7505.name: Godswill Akpabio
a7505.title: Senate President of Nigeria
a7505.speech: said the National Security Adviser and the heads of the NIA and SSS will appear before the lawmakers in a closed-door session to verify the allegations ; stressed the importance of hearing directly from the security agencies because classified intelligence is not for public discussion: "They will have information on past arrests, and security data is not what we can discuss in the market. We need to invite the security agencies because they will have the data."

a7505.speaker: Scott Perry, US Congressman
a7505.name: Scott Perry
a7505.title: US Congressman
a7505.speech: claimed that USAID funded terrorist organisations such as the Islamic State, al-Qaeda, and their affiliates, including Boko Haram in Nigeria ; alleged that USAID's annual budget of $697 million, including cash payments to Islamic schools (madrasas), may have inadvertently financed extremist training camps and terror groups.

a7505.speaker: Ali Ndume, Borno South Senator
a7505.name: Ali Ndume
a7505.title: Borno South Senator
a7505.speech: lamented the persistent threat posed by Boko Haram despite the federal government's financial investments in counter-terrorism operations ; stressed the urgent need to determine the validity of the allegations regarding USAID funding ; prayed the Senate to invite the NSA and the DGs of NIA and SSS over the matter.

a7505.speaker: Kaka Shehu, Borno Central Senator
a7505.name: Kaka Shehu
a7505.title: Borno Central Senator
a7505.speech: noted that previous ad hoc committees of the National Assembly had investigated Boko Haram's operations without effectively curbing their activities.

a7505.speaker: Abdul Ningi, Bauchi Central Senator
a7505.name: Abdul Ningi
a7505.title: Bauchi Central Senator
a7505.speech: also emphasised the necessity of compelling security heads to clarify the matter.

a7505.speaker: US Embassy in Nigeria
a7505.name: US Embassy in Nigeria
a7505.speech: stated that it would investigate all financial assistance provided to Nigeria under the USAID intervention.
